# SIMF Decisions Log

Implementation decisions and assumptions that are not (or not yet) captured in a
controlled document. Each entry is dated and explains the reasoning, per the
project working rules. Newest first.

When a decision is later absorbed into a controlled document, the entry keeps a
note pointing to that document.

| ID | Date | Decision | Reasoning |
|----|------|----------|-----------|
| D-503 | 2026-06-26 | **Exhibitor Excel export/import now round-trips the D-498 `Tier`.** The exhibitor sibling of D-502 (same "Excel IO omits a contract field" class, surfaced by the D-501 review). The grid export row `AdminExhibitorSummary` did not carry `Tier`, the export `_columns` never emitted it, and the insert-only import never read it — so the D-498/Wave-3 exhibitor tier could not be set or surfaced through Excel. **Fix:** `AdminExhibitorSummary` += optional `ExhibitorTier? Tier = null`; `AdminExhibitorService.ListAllAsync` projects `c.Tier`; `ExportExhibitorsEndpoint` appends a `Tier` column written by display name (`row.Tier?.ToString()` → Premium/Gold/Silver/Bronze, blank when null); `ImportExhibitorsEndpoint.ApplyRowAsync` parses an optional `Tier` cell into `CreateExhibitorRequest.Tier` via a new `ParseTier` (display name **or** raw int 10/20/30/40; **blank → null** since the tier is optional; unknown non-blank → per-row `DataValidationException`, not a batch abort). Required headers unchanged (`NameEn`/`NameAr`). **Tests:** `ExhibitorsExcelTests.Excel_round_trips_the_tier` (import a Tier workbook → the list summary carries it → export re-emits the column) + `Import_reports_a_per_row_error_for_an_unknown_tier` (blank tier still creates; "Diamond" → one error). E2E `cp-admin-exhibitors.md` E2E-EXH-024. Verified ExhibitorsExcelTests 6/6. Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | Identical reasoning to D-502 applied to the exhibitor module: the bulk-management surface must carry the tier or an export→edit→re-import silently drops it. Extending the existing grid summary (the established export source) over a separate projection keeps "one clear way"; the tier is the only D-498 field the Excel path missed (city lives on the linked Contact and is set via Edit, like ContactId). Making the column optional with a **blank-means-null** parse honours the tier being optional on the entity, while an unknown non-blank value is a genuine data error and so surfaces as a per-row error exactly like the sponsor `ParseTier`. |
| D-502 | 2026-06-26 | **Sponsor Excel export/import now round-trips the bilingual `Tagline`/`TaglineArabic` + `About`/`AboutArabic`.** Same class as D-501 (an IO layer omitting contract fields), surfaced by the D-501 review. The grid export row `AdminSponsorSummary` did not even carry these four fields and the export `_columns` / import `ApplyRowAsync` never emitted/read them, so the bilingual tagline + about could not round-trip through Excel (export hid them; insert-only import always created rows with them null). **Fix:** `AdminSponsorSummary` += 4 optional params (`Tagline`/`TaglineArabic`/`About`/`AboutArabic`, default null); `AdminSponsorService.ListAllAsync` projects them; `ExportSponsorsEndpoint` appends 4 columns (after `IsActive`, so existing column order is unchanged — import binds by header name); `ImportSponsorsEndpoint.ApplyRowAsync` reads the 4 optional cells into `AdminCreateSponsorRequest` (which already trims + length-guards them). The required-header set is unchanged (`NameEn`/`NameAr`/`Tier`) — the four are optional columns. `ContactId` stays out (a directory FK can't be plain text, as before). **Tests:** `SponsorsExcelTests.Export_includes_the_tagline_and_about_columns` (parses the workbook, asserts the 4 headers + the Tagline value) + `Import_round_trips_the_tagline_and_about` (imports the 4 columns, asserts the listed summary carries them). E2E `cp-admin-sponsors.md` E2E-SPN-026. Verified SponsorsExcelTests + SponsorsTests 14/14. Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | Excel is the bulk-management surface for sponsors; dropping the bilingual tagline + about at the IO boundary means an export→edit→re-import silently strips them — exactly the data-loss class D-501 fixed for the PUT path. Extending the existing grid-summary row (the established place export sources its columns, already carrying export-only fields like LogoRelativePath/Url) is the smallest fix that follows "one clear way", versus inventing a separate export projection. The extra summary columns cost a negligible grid fetch (sponsors number in the tens) and are not rendered as grid columns. Making the four columns optional (not required headers) keeps existing workbooks valid while letting a richer workbook round-trip the full sponsor. |
| D-501 | 2026-06-26 | **Sponsor edit no longer wipes the bilingual tagline — the admin update endpoint's inline bind model was missing `Tagline`/`TaglineArabic`.** Standalone data-loss fix flagged under Wave 3 (D-498). Root cause: the `PUT /admin/sponsors/{id}` endpoint binds an **inline** `UpdateSponsorRequest` model (defined in `SponsorEndpoints.cs`, separate from the contract `AdminUpdateSponsorRequest` because the route needs an `Id` property) which carried `About`/`AboutArabic` but **not** `Tagline`/`TaglineArabic`. So FastEndpoints silently dropped the `tagline`/`taglineArabic` JSON the CP form already sent, and `AdminSponsorService.UpdateAsync` (which does `sponsor.Tagline = NormaliseTagline(request.Tagline)`) then overwrote the stored tagline with **null** on every edit — the tagline could only be set at create and was lost the first time anyone edited the sponsor. (Create was unaffected: it binds the contract `AdminCreateSponsorRequest` directly.) **Fix (one file):** added `Tagline`/`TaglineArabic` to the inline `UpdateSponsorRequest` + the two mapping lines into `AdminUpdateSponsorRequest`. No contract / service / CP / entity / schema change (the contract, service mapping and CP form were already correct). **Regression test:** `tests/SIMF.Api.Tests/SponsorsTests.cs` → `Admin_update_preserves_the_tagline` — drives the **HTTP bind layer** (create with a tagline → PUT an edit that resends it → assert it round-trips); fails before the fix (tagline returns null), passes after. A service-level test would not catch it because the drop is at binding, not in `UpdateAsync`. E2E catalogue `cp-admin-sponsors.md` gains `E2E-SPN-025`. **Note (NOT fixed here, one-issue-per-change):** whether the analogous exhibitor update path has the same inline-model drift is unverified and out of scope for this fix. Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | An endpoint's inline bind model must stay in sync with its contract DTO; this is exactly the drift that happens when it doesn't — `About` was threaded through in Wave 3 but the earlier D-432 `Tagline` was never added to this inline model, so the field was accepted on the wire and silently discarded. The fix is the minimal two-property addition (not a refactor to bind the contract directly, which can't carry the route `Id`), and the regression test is deliberately at the HTTP layer because that is where the data was being lost. |
| D-500 | 2026-06-26 | **الطلبات unified requests feed (Wave 5) — one app screen over five request kinds + two new request types + self-cancel; supersedes the read-only My-meetings screen (additive migration `D500`).** New mobile screen **`requests`** (route name `requests`, path `/requests`, `RouteNames.requests` → `RequestsScreen`, Figma node `1408:9726`), **approved-account only**, reached from My-Area (the "meetings" stat tile + an "الطلبات" More row). It unifies **five** request kinds in one feed — `SpeakerMeeting`, `DelegationMeeting` (read-only), `SessionAttendance` (surfaced from the user's seat bookings, **not** cancellable here), `ParticipationDocument` (new) and `BadgeUpdate` (new) — with a "طلب جديد" submit button, status filter chips with counts (الكل / قيد المراجعة / مقبول / مرفوض / ملغى), and expandable cards; the user can **cancel** their **own pending** speaker/document/badge requests (confirm → toast). **APIs (all approved-only):** `GET /app/my-requests` → `AppRequestItem { kind, id, title, titleArabic, status, eventDateUtc?, createdAt, canCancel }[]`; `POST /app/document-requests` (`{ documentType: int (0 = AttendanceCertificate, 1 = ParticipationLetter, 2 = InvitationLetter), note?: ≤ 1000 }`); `POST /app/badge-requests` (`{ requestedJobTitle: 1–128 required, note?: ≤ 1000 }` — on admin **Accept** the title is applied to the user's profile `JobTitle`); `POST /app/my-requests/cancel` (`{ kind: int, id: guid }` — only own pending speaker(0)/document(3)/badge(4); delegation(1)/session-attendance(2) → 409). **CP desks (mirror `/admin/speaker-meeting-requests`):** `/admin/document-requests` (`DocumentRequestsList.razor`, perm `ParticipationDocumentRequests.View` list/open + `.Manage` respond; `POST /admin/document-requests/list`, `GET /admin/document-requests/{id}`, `PUT /admin/document-requests/{id}/respond`) and `/admin/badge-requests` (`BadgeRequestsList.razor`, perm `BadgeUpdateRequests.View`/`.Manage`; `POST /admin/badge-requests/list`, `GET /admin/badge-requests/{id}`, `PUT /admin/badge-requests/{id}/respond`); each is a SimfDataGrid + a Respond modal (Accept/Reject + optional note ≤ 2000), only Pending rows show Respond, respond with status = Pending → 400, and the detail/respond reveals the requester email (resolved on read). **Status:** `MeetingRequestStatus` gains `Cancelled = 3` (قيد المراجعة / مقبول / مرفوض / ملغى) — additive value, persisted by name. **Schema (additive on `SimfAppDbContext`, migration `D500`):** two new tables `ParticipationDocumentRequests` + `BadgeUpdateRequests` (requester = bare-Guid logical FK, status, note, response note, timestamps); Identity schema untouched. **Error codes:** `PARTICIPATION_DOCUMENT_REQUEST_INVALID` / `_NOT_FOUND` / `_STATUS_INVALID`; `BADGE_UPDATE_REQUEST_INVALID` / `_NOT_FOUND` / `_STATUS_INVALID`; `APP_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` (404, cancel target not owned); `APP_REQUEST_NOT_CANCELLABLE` (409, non-cancellable kind or not pending). **Bilingual toasts:** submit "تم إرسال طلبك"/"Your request was submitted" + "تعذّر إرسال الطلب"/"Could not submit the request"; cancel "تم إلغاء الطلب"/"Request cancelled" + "تعذّر إلغاء الطلب"/"Could not cancel the request". **Removed:** the D-479 read-only "My meetings" screen + `GET /app/my-meetings` endpoint + contract + its catalogue file (`mobile-my-meetings.md`, `E2E-MMM-*`) are superseded and deleted. **Tests:** `tests/SIMF.Api.Tests/MyRequestsTests.cs` + `ParticipationDocumentRequestsTests.cs` + `BadgeUpdateRequestsTests.cs`. DoD trio shipped (PAGE-INDEX + `mobile-requests.md` `E2E-REQ-001..011` + `cp-document-requests.md` `E2E-CPDR-001..008` + `cp-badge-requests.md` `E2E-CPBR-001..008` + this entry). **D-110 freeze:** additive tables under the D-219 wave-lift (re-instate before handover). Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | The old My-meetings screen showed only two read-only kinds and offered no action, while the audience also needed to **ask** for documents and badge corrections and to **drop** a pending request — so one **unified الطلبات feed** keyed on a small `AppRequestItem` projection (a single list endpoint with a `kind` discriminator + a per-row `canCancel`) is the reusable shape, replacing the narrower screen rather than bolting parallel screens on. The **VIP/session attendance row reuses the existing seat-bookings** (owner decision) instead of a new attendance-request entity — a session "attendance request" *is* a seat booking, so there is no second source of truth and nothing to keep in sync (D-157); it is therefore read-only on this screen (managed from the seat screens) and a cancel attempt is correctly a 409. The two genuinely new request types each need their own row + state, so they are **dedicated additive tables** (`ParticipationDocumentRequests`, `BadgeUpdateRequests`) following the established `SpeakerMeetingRequest` pattern; mirroring `/admin/speaker-meeting-requests` for both desks (SimfDataGrid + Respond modal, list-omits-email PII, Pending-only Respond, status-invalid guard) keeps "one clear way" and reuses the proven review-queue UX. Adding **`Cancelled = 3`** to `MeetingRequestStatus` (additive, persisted by name) is the minimal way to model a user-initiated drop without a new enum, and self-cancel is scoped to **own + pending + the three submittable kinds** so a user can never cancel another user's request (404) or a row that is not theirs to drop (409). Applying the badge title to `JobTitle` **on Accept** keeps the badge the single rendered source and makes the admin decision the one authoritative write. |
| D-499 | 2026-06-26 | **Delegations screen (الوفود) — invited-country delegations with head + dates (Wave 4 — new public app screen + endpoint; all-on-Country schema, additive migration `D499`).** New mobile screen **#21 `delegations`** (route name `delegations`, path `/delegations`, Figma node `1426:10771`) — **restored** (the screen was removed in D-277) and rebuilt as a **public, anonymous** browse surface reached from a home tile + the direct route. It lists the **invited** countries' delegations: a stats strip (participating-countries count + total-participants count), a search box (filters by country name ar/en + head name ar/en), and one card per invited country (flag, bilingual country name, head of delegation = name + job title + an initial avatar, an arrival→departure date range, and a member count). **API (new, public):** `GET /api/v1/app/delegations` (`AllowAnonymous`) → `AppDelegations { countryCount, totalParticipants, items[] }`, each `AppDelegationItem { countryId, countryCode, countryName, countryNameArabic, headName?, headNameArabic?, headTitle?, arrivalDate?, departureDate?, memberCount }` — projects only invited + active countries (`Country.IsInvited`), resolves the head from the new `Country.HeadOfDelegationUserProfileId` pointer, and computes `memberCount` as the active delegate `UserProfile`s (`IsDelegate && IsActive`) with that `NationalityId`. **CP:** the existing Country Add/Edit form (`/admin/countries`, `CountriesList` → `CountryAddEdit.razor`) now also sets the delegation **arrival/departure dates** + a **head-of-delegation picker** (an active delegate of the country, fed by a new admin sub-endpoint `GET /api/v1/admin/countries/{id}/delegates`, gated `Countries.View`); the dates + head save through the existing `PUT /admin/countries/{id}`, **permissions unchanged** (`Countries.View`/`.Create`/`.Edit`/`.Delete`). **Schema (additive on `SimfAppDbContext`, migration `D499`):** `Country` gains `DelegationArrivalDate` + `DelegationDepartureDate` (date, nullable) + `HeadOfDelegationUserProfileId` (`Guid`, nullable FK → `UserProfile`, `SetNull`). Identity schema untouched. **Incidental fix:** the country **Update** binding model previously **dropped `IsInvited`** on PUT (it was not threaded through) — now carried through so a delegations-relevant edit can't silently clear the invited flag. **Bilingual copy:** title "الوفود"/"Delegations", search hint "ابحث عن دولة أو وفد..."/"Search for a country or delegation...", stats "دولة مشاركة"/"Participating countries" + "إجمالي المشاركين"/"Total participants", head label "رئيس الوفد"/"Head of delegation", error "تعذر تحميل الوفود."/"Could not load delegations.", empty "لا توجد وفود بعد."/"No delegations yet.". DoD trio shipped (PAGE-INDEX + `mobile-delegations.md` E2E `E2E-DEL-001..009` + this entry). **D-110 freeze:** additive `Country` columns under the D-219 wave-lift (re-instate before handover). Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | The delegation's head, dates and "invited" flag all describe the **country**, so putting them **on `Country`** (two date columns + a head pointer) is the single, natural management surface — one CP form edits everything about an invited country in one place, and a single FK **enforces exactly one head** per country. Storing the head as a `UserProfileId` **pointer** (rather than an `IsHeadOfDelegation` flag on the profile) makes "who leads this delegation" a country-owned fact that can't drift into two profiles both claiming the role, and `SetNull` means deactivating that profile simply clears the head, never orphans the country. The **member count stays derived on read** (active delegates by `NationalityId`) per D-157 — no duplicated/denormalized count to keep in sync. **Public/anonymous** access is consistent with the other public event-content endpoints (speakers, booths, sponsors): delegation participation is branding/event information, carries no secret, and must load for guests. Restoring screen #21 (vs inventing a new number) keeps the mockup numbering stable. The `IsInvited`-on-PUT fix is in-scope because the delegations feed keys on that flag — an edit that dropped it would quietly hide a country from the screen. |
| D-496 | 2026-06-25 | **Dynamic, config-driven rating system — replaces the fixed single-row `Rating` with admin-defined rating types → question groups → questions, and normalized responses → answers; adds an end-of-session "rate this session" notification with an in-app deep-link.** Owner directive: make ratings dynamic (admin adds questions, optionally grouped e.g. Speaker/Sound/Light; a per-type "allow comment" toggle; a stars-only mode), organised by **type** (App, Session, …, admin-creatable), with the app now showing **two** ratings — App (global, from the More menu) and Session (per session, at session end). Four owner decisions taken with it: **(1) admin-creatable types** — `App`+`Session` seeded as un-deletable **system** types, each with a `Scope` (`Global` = once per user vs `PerSession` = once per user per session); **(2) drop and start fresh** — the old fixed `Rating` table/entity/contracts/endpoints/UI are removed (existing rating rows discarded); **(3) seat-holders at session end** — a new `SessionRatingPromptWorker` (mirrors `SessionReminderWorker`) fires when `Session.EndUtc` passes within a 6-hour back-fill window and notifies active-seat attendees, deduped on the new additive nullable `Session.RatingPromptSentUtc`; **(4) derive the deep-link from kind + entity** — one additive `NotificationKind.SessionRatingRequest = 45` reusing the existing `Notification.RelatedEntityType="Session"`/`RelatedEntityId`, **no Notification schema change**, and the Flutter app gains tap-routing (the `NotificationItem` model, which had been dropping `relatedEntityId`/`relatedEntityType`, now decodes them). **Schema (additive-plus-drop on `SimfAppDbContext`, migration `App/20260625072139_D496_DynamicRatings`):** drop `Ratings`; add `RatingTypes` (unique `Code`, `Scope` int, `HasOverallStars`/`AllowComment`/`IsSystem` flags, optional comment labels), `RatingQuestionGroups`, `RatingQuestions` (nullable group FK, `SetNull` so deleting a group leaves its questions flat), `RatingResponses` (header — `UserId` bare-Guid logical FK; `TargetId` = session id or `Guid.Empty` sentinel for global so the unique `(UserId,RatingTypeId,TargetId)` index stays uniform; nullable `OverallStars` + `Comment`), `RatingAnswers` (line — 1–5 per question, unique `(ResponseId,QuestionId)`); + `Session.RatingPromptSentUtc`. Identity schema untouched. **Seeding** is a runtime `RatingSeeder` (not migration `InsertData`) called from `Program.cs` (all envs) **and** the test fixture — App (Global, stars+comment) + Session (PerSession, stars+comment, default non-required Speaker/Sound/Light questions). **API:** app `GET /app/feedback/form` (resolve by code/id + optional target, prefill from existing) + `POST /app/feedback/submit` (upsert; service validates scope→target, overall-required-when-`HasOverallStars`, required-question coverage, answer-belongs-to-type); admin `RatingConfigEndpoints` (types/groups/questions CRUD, system-type delete blocked 400, gated by new `RatingConfig.{View,Create,Edit,Delete}`) + the responses grid + `…/ratings/kpi` (per-type response-count/avg + per-question avg) gated `Ratings.View` + the XLSX export gated `Ratings.Export`. **CP:** new `/admin/rating-config` (FaqManager-style three-level master-detail) + the rewritten `/admin/ratings` (responses grid + per-type KPI stat cards) + nav item + bilingual resx. **App:** the `rate_screen` is now a dynamic server-driven form (overall + grouped/flat questions + comment), App-rating from the More menu, Session-rating reached via the notification deep-link. **Tests:** rewritten `FeedbackRatingsTests`, new `RatingConfigTests` + `SessionRatingPromptWorkerTests`; backend compiles 0-error, `flutter analyze` clean. **FREEZE NOTE:** dropping a table + adding five is a **structural** change beyond the D-219 additive lift — taken pre-handover with owner awareness; the schema freeze must be re-instated before the production publish, and backend + app must ship together (the old `/app/feedback/rate` wire contract is removed). Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | The fixed `Rating` baked four element scores into the schema/contract/CP/Excel/app — five places to touch per question change. Making questions/groups/comment-toggle **data** (types → groups → questions; responses → answers) is the reusable, owner-requested shape, and a header+line response model gives clean per-type/per-question KPIs while preserving the original "one rating per user (now per target), upsert" behaviour. The four decisions were the genuine forks: admin-creatable types with a `Scope` is the most flexible reading of "dynamic" while keeping App vs per-session distinct; drop-and-start-fresh is safe pre-handover and avoids carrying a dead table; reusing the worker + the pre-existing `RelatedEntityType`/`Id` (which the entity comment already anticipated) delivers the deep-link with the smallest, most freeze-friendly surface — one additive enum value, no Notification schema change. The `Guid.Empty` target sentinel is the deliberate guard against SQL Server treating NULLs as distinct (which would let a user rate "App" repeatedly). Runtime seeding (vs migration `InsertData`) matches `IdentitySeeder` and guarantees the built-in types exist in prod and in the test host. The structural drop is recorded as a freeze-lift with the re-instate-before-handover and ship-together caveats so it is not mistaken for a routine additive change. |
| D-495 | 2026-06-24 | **Organization / About profile — a normalized, admin-editable, edition-generic forum-config record (new App schema + cached conditional-GET API + CP editor + app About screen); the old SiteSettings social/welcome keys migrated into it.** Owner approved a single source of truth for the forum's "project/about" data (name, title, slogan, bio, version + dates, **event start/end**, **current year**, **status** = Soon/Open/Archived, location + GPS, contact phone/email/website, **main live-stream YouTube link**, 7 social links, logo, plus the variable *about-items* `<title,text>` and *details* `<name,value>` lists). **Schema (additive on `SimfAppDbContext`, under the D-199/211/219 App freeze-lift; Identity untouched, migration `App/20260624181539_D495`):** singleton `OrganizationProfile` (fixed `SingletonId`, `BaseAuditEntity` so `UpdatedAt` drives the cache token) + 2 child tables `OrganizationAboutItems` / `OrganizationDetails`; **social links are 7 fixed columns** (the shipped `SiteSocialLinks` wire contract) and the **single website is `ContactWebsite`** (not child tables — KISS for a fixed/known set, owner-chosen over key/value EAV and over per-list child tables); new `ForumStatus` enum + `AssetCategory.OrganizationLogo=7` (append-only). **Storage decision:** DB-as-source-of-truth, **not** a server `setting.json` file (admin-edits-in-prod need transactions/audit/backup/no-deploy-clobber); the API returns the whole profile as one JSON doc the app caches. **Caching / freshness:** `IMemoryCache` read service (copies `GateConfigCache`, 5-min TTL + invalidate-on-write) behind the **D-173 `Last-Modified`/`If-Modified-Since`→304** conditional-GET (the app's "GetSetting(version)" revalidation, done the codebase-blessed way — the editable `Version` field stays display data). **One source of truth:** the 9 `SiteSettingKeys` (`social.*` + `registration.successMessage.*`) are copied into the singleton columns by the migration then soft-deactivated; `SiteSettingsService.GetAsync` + `AdminSystemSettingService.SaveSiteSettingsAsync` are repointed at the singleton, keeping the exact `SiteSettingsResponse` shape so the website footer / app / `SimfPublicClient` are unchanged. **Security:** public `GET /app/organization-profile` is `AllowAnonymous` (branding must load pre-login) but hardened — whitelist projection (no audit cols), http(s)-only URL sanitisation on read (D-467), all writes gated by `OrganizationProfile.Manage` + approved account + audited (`OrganizationProfile.Updated`), logo via the existing AV-scanned `Asset` pipeline; `AssetPermissionRegistry` maps the new category. **Permission** `OrganizationProfile.View/.Manage` seeded (idempotent, AdminOnly) gating API + CP. **CP:** `/admin/organization-profile` editor (full-document GET+PUT; scalar form + 7 social + inline about/detail rows), nav item, BFF passthroughs, bilingual resx. **App:** `OrgProfile` model + an app-lifetime `orgProfileProvider` (`Notifier<OrgProfile?>`) **loaded at the splash, persisted to `shared_preferences`, hydrated synchronously from disk (instant on every page, offline-safe), and revalidated with a `Last-Modified`/304 conditional GET** (new `SimfApiClient.getConditional`) — the owner's "load at first time, cache through the run, version-check" model. It data-drives the existing About screen (name → title → about-items as the vision/mission cards → details list) with the static l10n as the fallback. **Seed = the real current 2026 edition** lifted from the app's previously-hardcoded l10n (forum name/title, mission+vision, year/date/location), so the table ships populated and the app re-skins from config. **Tests:** `OrganizationProfileTests` (anonymous read, **304**, admin 403-gate, admin save+reflect, URL-reject) + `SiteSettingsPublicTests`/`SiteSettingsAdminTests` repointed + `about_screen_test` provider-override — all green; CP nav-permission test green. **Follow-ups (NOT in this changeset):** full edition-generic sweep of the remaining hardcoded app locations (home live-stream link / status badge — the About screen + the shared provider are done); a CP logo-upload widget (logo is `Asset`-backed but the upload control is not wired yet); retire the now-redundant `/admin/site-settings` page; system-wide rotating-TOTP app-key enforcement on the public surface. Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | The data is fixed-and-known (one record + two small lists), admin-editable in production, and consumed identically by app + website across every edition — so the right shape is a **normalized typed singleton + child tables in the DB**, not a key/value EAV bag (no type safety / validation / clean projection) and not a server file (no transactions/audit/backup, clobbered on deploy). Social/website stay columns because the set is fixed by the shipped wire contract — a child table would add ordering/EAV cost for no gain. Migrating the 9 keys into it (rather than leaving two stores) preserves "one clear way" while keeping the public `SiteSettingsResponse` byte-compatible so nothing downstream breaks. The public read is anonymous by necessity (pre-login branding) but carries no secret — its security is projection + write-auth + sanitisation + cache/304, not a password; a leaked anonymous call can only scrape public branding. `Last-Modified`/304 reuses the only blessed cache-revalidation pattern in the codebase (D-173) and matches the owner's version-check intent exactly. Seeding from the existing l10n makes the migration a faithful "lift hardcoded content into config" rather than inventing copy. The app loads the config at the splash, persists it locally, and shares it app-wide — hydrated from disk synchronously so it survives cold starts and renders offline — and revalidates with the codebase's `Last-Modified`/304 pattern, which is exactly the owner's "load at first time, cache through the run, GetSetting(version)" requirement. The broader hardcoded-location sweep + the other items are deferred as separable follow-ups, recorded here so they aren't lost. |

Returns `{ CooldownSeconds: 60 }`. **App:** `AuthController.resendOtp()` (reads the otpToken from `AwaitingOtp`, no state change) → repo/api `resendOtp`; the screen's resend re-issues in place + restarts the 60s countdown + toasts, errors inline. **Verified:** API build 0/0; **`ResendOtpTests` 4/4** (reissue-verifies-against-same-ticket, old-code-invalidated, unknown-ticket→400, capped→429) + auth-flow **62/62**; `simf_auth_pkg` **44/44** (+2 controller cases); **full app suite 555/555**; analyze clean. **Independent security review: MERGE-READY, no Critical/High/Medium/Low** (the AttemptCount-preservation invariant + the per-account cap are the load-bearing controls). SIMF-API-001 Amendment A.1 + E2E `mobile-sign-in` E2E-MOB003-020 updated. Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | A "Resend" that navigates away is a poor flow; the owner wants it in place. Reusing `GetValidTicketAsync` + `IssueSignInOtpAsync` means the resend inherits the exact ticket validation, hashing, per-hour cap and audit of the sign-in OTP. The ticket-window refresh is required (code outlives the ticket otherwise) but the attempt counter is held monotonic so the window-extension can't be turned into extra guesses — the security review confirmed this is the invariant that keeps the brute-force budget flat at 5/10^6. |
| D-489 | 2026-06-21 | **#9 — "Keep me logged in" now actually gates session persistence (was email-prefill only).** The report: with the checkbox **off**, the session still survived an app restart. Before, the remember-me flag (D-360) gated only the last-email prefill; the session was **always** written to secure storage and restored on cold start. Fix (client-side, in `AuthController`): a new `_rememberSession` flag set per sign-in (`signIn({…, bool rememberSession = true})`, passed from the sign-in screen's checkbox). When **false**, `_persistSession` **clears** the stored auth values and returns instead of writing — so the session lives in memory ONLY: it works for the running app (the 401-refresh reads the in-memory `_refreshToken`, not storage) but a restart's `_restoreFromStorage` finds nothing → signed out. A **biometric (device-key) re-open always sets it true** (the device key is an explicit "remember me on this device"). The device key + prefs are untouched by `clearAuthValues` (StorageKeys note). **Verified:** `flutter analyze` clean; **full app suite 555/555**; `simf_auth_pkg` **42/42** incl. 2 new `auth_controller_signin_test` cases (un-remembered → no `refreshToken` write + `clearAuthValues` called; remembered → persisted). App-side only; **no backend** (there is no server session-scoped token — the client enforces the lifetime). Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | "Keep me logged in" must mean what it says. The backend issues the same refresh token regardless, so session-vs-persistent is a **client** decision — enforced by not writing to durable storage when unchecked (the standard "session cookie" semantics). Doing it in `_persistSession` covers every persist path (sign-in, OTP, refresh, hydrate) in one place; the running session is unaffected because refresh already uses the in-memory token. Biometric re-open is exempted because enrolling a device key IS the user opting into persistence on that device. No new storage key was needed — the flag is in-memory, and on restart there is simply nothing to restore. |

| D-481 | 2026-06-20 | **Auth-refresh self-deadlock fixed — a 401-from-refresh no longer hangs the request (root cause of the live Rate-submit infinite spinner).** The 401 refresh-and-retry path (`SimfApiClient._execute`) routed the refresh call (`AuthApi.refresh` → `POST /app/auth/refresh`) through **itself**: a 401 on refresh (expired / reuse-detected refresh token, or a session past the D-443 24h absolute cap) re-entered the single-flight `AuthController.refresh()`, whose `_refreshInFlight ??=` handed back the **same in-flight future the refresh was running inside** → it awaited itself → permanent deadlock; the request and its UI spinner hung forever (seen live on the Rate submit ~10 min after sign-in). The `_extraSkipRefresh` marker meant to prevent re-entry was set but **never read**. **Fix (both vendored `simf_data_pkg` + `simf_auth_pkg` copies):** (1) `_execute` now honors the marker — skips the 401-refresh when `response.requestOptions.extra[_extraSkipRefresh] == true` (also stops the post-refresh retry from looping on a second 401); (2) `SimfApiClient.post` gains `skipAuthRefresh`, set by `AuthApi.refresh`, so the refresh call's own 401 surfaces as a normal `ApiFailure` → `AuthFailure` → `refresh()` returns false → clean sign-out, no deadlock. A 20s `_refreshBounded` net (commit `b50d920`) stays as defence-in-depth. **Regression test** `api_client_refresh_test`: a 401-on-refresh resolves to an `ApiFailure` with the single-flight refresh running **exactly once** — it deadlocks/times-out without the fix. **Verified:** `flutter analyze` clean; data-pkg tests **12/12**; app builds. Commits `b50d920` + `eeb2b39c`. App-side only (ships in the app build; no API redeploy). Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split`. | A request that can never settle is worse than one that fails — the user gets an endless spinner with no recourse. Honoring the marker + tagging the refresh call removes the re-entry **at the source**; the bounded await guarantees liveness even if some other refresh path stalls later. Fixing both vendored copies keeps them from drifting (the app builds against `simf_app/packages`). |

| D-454 | 2026-06-19 | **App font switched to the Figma type — Inter (Latin) + Cairo (Arabic), app-wide.** Owner: "the font in app not as in figma." Owner chose **Inter + Cairo Arabic** (AskUserQuestion). Implemented as a **font-fallback chain** (one theme switch, no per-widget locale logic): bundled the two OFL **variable** fonts (`Inter[opsz,wght].ttf` + `Cairo[slnt,wght].ttf` → `assets/fonts/Inter.ttf` / `Cairo.ttf`; Flutter maps `fontWeight` onto the `wght` axis), registered both families in `pubspec.yaml`, and set `SimfTheme.fontFamily='Inter'` + `fontFamilyFallback=['Cairo']` on all four ThemeData (light / dark / HC-light / HC-dark) + the AppBar title style. Inter has no Arabic glyphs, so every Arabic character falls through to Cairo automatically while Latin/digits stay Inter — exactly the frame split. `app_theme.dart` is the single switch point (grep confirms no other `fontFamily`/hardcoded family anywhere in the app). IBM Plex stays bundled but unreferenced (left for a later cleanup — not deleted, to keep the diff minimal + avoid the concurrent session). Verified: `flutter pub get` + `flutter analyze` clean; **full `simf_app` suite 515/515 green** (no layout regressions — the D-436 RTL position tests use relative `dx`, robust to metric shifts); debug APK built + installed + **live-rendered on the emulator** — the sign-in screen now shows Arabic in Cairo + Latin in Inter, variable weights mapping correctly (bold heading, regular labels), zero tofu. The **auth flow's logic/layout stays frozen** — only the inherited global font changed (the owner's app-wide directive). Renumbered D-452→D-454 (a concurrent worker took D-452/453). Branch `feature/app-cp-api-split` (push ≠ deploy). | Owner wants the app to match the Figma type, and the frames use Inter + Cairo. A fallback chain (Inter→Cairo) is the idiomatic Flutter way to get "Latin in font A, Arabic in font B" from one setting — no locale branching, works for mixed-script strings, and is inherited by every TextStyle. Variable fonts are what Google Fonts ships for both, and Flutter's `fontWeight`→`wght` mapping covers the 400/500/600/700 the design uses. Keeping IBM Plex bundled (vs deleting four files + the pubspec block) keeps this change small and avoids racing the concurrent session on shared core files. The global font is a theme concern, not auth-flow logic, so the freeze is intact. |

| D-443 | 2026-06-19 | **Token lifetimes hardened to the NCA caps + token-driven session-expiry UX (App + CP + Web).** A security review rejected the prior lifetimes (access token 30 min; refresh token 30 days) and mandated **access ≤ 5 min** and **session ≤ 1 day**. Built: **(A)** `Jwt:AccessTokenMinutes` 30→**5** and a new `Jwt:SessionLifetimeHours`=**24** (`JwtOptions`), exposed as `IJwtTokenService.RefreshTokenLifetime` so the Application layer reads it without a new package reference. **(B)** the refresh token is now capped at an **absolute 24h from sign-in, not a sliding window** — the three issue sites (`SignInService`, `DeviceKeyService`, `SessionService`) were unified on the config value, and **rotation carries the chain's original `ExpiresAt` forward** (`SessionService.RefreshAsync` → `ExpiresAt = presented.ExpiresAt`), so a user who keeps refreshing is still forced to re-sign-in at 24h. **No schema change** — the existing `RefreshToken.ExpiresAt` column already holds the deadline, so the D-110 freeze is untouched. **(C)** token-driven warning UX: the short access token is rotated **silently** in the background while the user is active; once idle, a bilingual (EN/AR, RTL) countdown modal ("Stay signed in / Sign out") appears ~1 min before the token lapses and signs the user out if ignored. CP (interactive) starts it via `SessionTimeoutGuard.razor` → `simfSessionGuard.start` JS interop; the Website (SSR) renders the localized config and the JS module auto-starts; both add a `GET /session/status` BFF endpoint that piggybacks on the existing D-121 cookie-refresh hook (`SimfCookieRefreshHandler`). **(D)** the Flutter app already silently refreshes on a 401 + replays once and routes to sign-in via `onSessionExpired`, so the new caps flow through it unchanged (the 24h cap surfaces as a clean re-login); a 5-min idle modal was deliberately **not** ported because idle ≠ session-end on mobile (open item: confirm whether a warn-before-24h-cap dialog is wanted in-app). Verified: backend + CP + Web build Release 0 warnings / 0 errors; new `RefreshAbsoluteCapTests` proves rotation does not slide past the 24h cap; `RefreshExpiryTests` updated 30d→24h. **Code-review fix:** the client guard now has a **single-flight** `fetchStatus` + **idempotent** `start()`, so the now-frequent 5-min-token refresh cannot fire two concurrent `/session/status` calls that would present the same refresh token and trip rotation reuse-detection (which would force-sign-out an active user + raise a false stolen-token alarm). **Live-test follow-up (the real root cause):** owner tested on the app and the 5-min token exposed that the **app had no single-flight refresh** — the home screen's parallel loads all 401 at once, each rotated the same refresh token, and the second rotation tripped server reuse-detection → the whole session was revoked, so the app sat on stale content showing "تعذر تحميل الرعاة" instead of renewing or going to login. Fixed at the source per OAuth/MSAL guidance: **(i)** `AuthController.refresh()` is now **single-flight** (concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh); **(ii)** `app.dart` routes a signed-in→signed-out transition to `/sign-in` so a session that dies on a public/Home screen lands on login (the route-gate already covered protected screens); the CP/Web JS guard got the same single-flight + idempotent-start earlier. **Decided AGAINST the backend reuse grace-window** (despite the earlier approval): now that the storms are fixed at the source it is redundant, and it would weaken the RFC-6819 reuse-detection control and contradict two existing security tests (`SessionTests.Reusing_a_rotated_refresh_token_revokes_the_whole_family` + `...writes_a_RefreshTokenReused_audit_entry`). `deploy/set-env-api.ps1` documents the two NCA-cap lifetimes. Note: the recording-stream token (`Jwt:StreamTokenMinutes`=180, distinct `simf-stream` audience, D-232) is intentionally independent and can outlive the 24h cap for read-only recording playback — not a cap violation. | Owner relayed the customer/NCA finding verbatim ("Not more than 5 minutes" / "Not more than 1 day") and chose **warning-modal-only + absolute 24h cap + token-driven** (AskUserQuestion, 2026-06-18/19). Carrying `ExpiresAt` forward (vs adding a `SessionExpiresAt` column) keeps the absolute cap inside the frozen schema. Reading the lifetime through `IJwtTokenService` avoids adding `Microsoft.Extensions.Options` to the `SIMF.Application` csproj (global rule §1.7 — no project-file edits without explicit request). A short access token rotated silently keeps active users signed in without interruption; the idle warning + auto-logout is the audit-defensible idle-session control the review asked for. |

| D-394 | 2026-06-13 | **The app's native HTTP client accepts the SIMF API host's self-signed certificate (owner-requested PoC bypass).** The production API (`https://simf_api.zagali-ict.com`) serves a self-signed cert that is in fact issued for the server's machine name (`CN`/`SAN = WIN-MAP9VAMAU4Q`), **not** the public hostname — so it fails BOTH CA-trust AND hostname verification, and the native `HttpClient` (dio) rejects every request (the web channel is unaffected — the browser owns TLS). On owner instruction ("the api is selfsign … fix app to bypass"), `installSelfSignedApiTlsBypass()` (in `lib/core/net/`, native-only via a conditional import; a no-op stub on web) installs an `HttpOverrides` whose `badCertificateCallback` accepts a bad cert **only for the configured API host** (`BuildConfig.apiBaseUrl`'s host) — every other host keeps full TLS validation, so the blast radius is exactly that one self-signed backend, not a blanket "accept any cert". **SECURITY:** this trades away MITM protection for the API host; it is a deliberate PoC trade-off while the backend serves a self-signed cert. **Remove it once the server presents a valid cert for its hostname** (rename the host to `simf-api.…` + a real/Let's-Encrypt cert, or a self-signed cert whose SAN is the real hostname). **Verified live:** a debug build on an Android emulator (`flutter run --dart-define=SIMF_API_BASE=https://simf_api.zagali-ict.com/api/v1`) reached the live API end-to-end — a sign-in round-trip completed and returned the server's `AUTH_WRONG_SURFACE_WEB` 403 (the superadmin is a CP account, correctly barred from the visitor surface), which proves TLS connectivity (a failed bypass would surface a handshake error, not a server response). The native `android/` folder, its launcher icon (`flutter_launcher_icons` → SIMF logo) and a `compileSdk = 36` bump (the toolchain's `flutter.compileSdkVersion` is 33; the plugins' androidx deps — core 1.18 / activity 1.12 / browser 1.9 — need 36) are **working-tree-only** — `android/`/`ios/` are git-ignored/generated, so only the Dart bypass + this entry are committed. | The owner explicitly accepted the self-signed-cert trade-off for the PoC and asked the app to bypass it. Scoping the accept to the single configured API host (not "accept any cert") keeps the weakening minimal and auditable, and the loud caveat + removal condition keep it from silently becoming permanent. The proper fix remains server-side (a valid certificate for the real hostname). |

| D-391 | 2026-06-13 | **CP — an API call that returns HTTP 401 now redirects the browser to the login page (centralised in the one JS API helper).** Owner request: "on cp when api return 401 redirect to login page." Audit (grep-verified) confirmed every authenticated CP→API call funnels through `window.simfAccount` in `wwwroot/js/simf-account.js` — there is no other `fetch(` in the CP, no other JS that hits the API, and no component calls the typed clients/`HttpClient` directly except the 5 pre-auth login pages (the login flow itself, where 401→login is moot). All `simfAccount` JSON helpers return via `simfReadEnvelope(response)`; the only non-envelope path is the binary `downloadXlsx`. So the fix is two spots: a `if (response.status === 401) { window.location.assign('/login'); … }` guard at the top of `simfReadEnvelope` (a never-resolving promise so the calling page doesn't act on a bogus body mid-navigation) and the same guard in `downloadXlsx`. This covers all browser→API calls in one place. **Option A (chosen by the owner over Option B):** the redirect is triggered in JS because, in this Blazor Server BFF design (D-017), API calls go out as a browser `fetch` to the CP's same-origin `/account/api/*` endpoints (so the JWT stays server-side in the cookie), and the 401 response is received in the browser — a server-side C# `DelegatingHandler` cannot redirect a browser sitting in a `fetch`. The cleaner "pure-C#/no-JS" alternative (Option B — move every CP data page's API call into the circuit via the typed clients + a single `DelegatingHandler` that calls `NavigationManager.NavigateTo("/login")` on 401) was considered and **deferred** as a large, separate refactor touching every CP page with real regression risk — disproportionate for a 401-redirect fix. A full-page `window.location.assign('/login')` is the equivalent of Blazor's `NavigateTo(forceLoad:true)`; `/login` is `[AllowAnonymous]` and does not bounce authenticated users, so there is no redirect loop. The server-side cookie-middleware change first sketched (turning the cookie's 302→/login into a 401 for `/account/api`, to also cover a fully-expired cookie) was dropped from scope — the owner scoped this strictly to "when the API returns 401." | The owner's explicit, narrowly-scoped request. Putting the redirect in the single shared JS helper is the minimum change that covers 100% of the authenticated CP→API surface (proven by the audit) without per-page edits, and is consistent with the shipped BFF architecture rather than re-architecting it. Option B is the more idiomatic Blazor approach but is a project-sized refactor; recording it here as the deferred alternative keeps the decision deliberate. No backend/API/schema change; CP-only, additive JS. |
| D-390 | 2026-06-13 | **Amends D-101 — the super-admin seeder NO LONGER force-re-enables two-factor on every boot.** The owner reported that disabling the super-admin's 2FA in the CP did not stick: a restart switched it back on. Root cause: the D-101 self-heal block in `IdentitySeeder.SeedAsync` ran `if (!admin.TwoFactorEnabled) SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(true)` on every startup (it fires whenever `SuperAdmin:TotpSecret` is configured, which it is). The empirical proof: a full migrate+seed restart against the live local `SIMF_Identity` left the super-admin row **byte-for-byte identical** when 2FA was already on (the block was a silent no-op), and the seeder log showed `seeded 0 of N` everywhere with no `"TwoFactorEnabled re-enabled"` line — confirming the flip only happens when the flag is found `false`. **Fix (option B2):** the TOTP-secret self-heal now runs ONLY while `admin.TwoFactorEnabled` is true — guard changed to `if (admin.TwoFactorEnabled && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(settings.TotpSecret))` — and the force-enable branch is deleted. 2FA is still enabled once, at first creation, in `CreateSuperAdminAsync`. Guarding the re-pin (not just removing the force-enable) matters because a real disable (`TotpEnrollmentService.DisableAsync`) **wipes the active authenticator key**; re-pinning it while 2FA is off would both resurrect an orphan secret and mutate the row on every boot. The original D-101 protection (config stays authoritative for the key so "TOTP not working" can't recur) is retained for the case it was written for — 2FA on but the stored key drifted from config. Regression test added (`IdentitySeederTests.SeedAsync_keeps_a_super_admin_2FA_disable_across_a_reseed`): disable + key-removal, re-seed, assert still disabled and key still null (capture/restore in `finally` so the shared class fixture's other tests still see 2FA on). | The owner's explicit choice ("let disable persist", reversing D-101). D-101 forced 2FA on to fix an earlier "second factor bypassed" complaint; the operator must still be able to turn it off deliberately and have that survive a restart. Self-healing the secret only when 2FA is on is the minimal change that both honours the operator's on/off choice and keeps the key authoritative when it is actually used — addressing the root cause (an unconditional force-enable) rather than the symptom. Identity schema unchanged (frozen, D-110); behaviour-only edit to one seeder block + one test. |

Root cause: `main.dart` overrode `authTokenSourceProvider` with `ref.read(authControllerProvider.notifier)` resolved **eagerly inside the provider graph** — a circular dependency (controller → repository → api client → token source → controller). Riverpod rejects the cycle (`CircularDependencyError` — it counts `read` edges too) and the recovery path left the interceptors with a notifier whose `build()` never ran (`LateInitializationError` internally; `currentAccessToken()` permanently null). **Not web-specific — the same wiring ships in the native app**; the authenticated happy path had never been live-driven end-to-end before this run (D-324 drove a failed sign-in only). **Fix:** new `AuthTokenBridge` in `simf_auth_pkg` — a passive `AuthTokenSource` with **no provider dependencies** installed via `authTokenSourceProvider.overrideWith((ref) => AuthTokenBridge())`; `AuthController.build()` registers itself as the delegate (the read goes controller → token source, the acyclic direction); until the controller builds, the bridge behaves like `NoAuthTokenSource` (correct pre-auth). The old `authTokenSourceFromController` helper (no consumers) was replaced. **Verification:** deterministic regression test `simf_app/test/app/auth_token_wiring_test.dart` — mirrors the main.dart wiring over a header-recording dio adapter replaying the real captured wire payloads; fails against the old wiring (CircularDependencyError), passes with the bridge (`Authorization: Bearer …` asserted on the hydration call). Suites: Flutter **347/347**, analyze clean (new `dio` dev-dependency for the test, same major as simf_data_pkg's pin). **Live re-proof:** release web rebuild → sign-in → users/me 200 → profile-completion route → full form → save → success → signed-in home (unread badge + avatar + visitor tiles) — `docs/SIMF-Wave1-E2E-Validation-2026-06-12.md` §4–§5. | The defect class is exactly what the owner's "real testing" mandate exists to catch: every unit/controller test passed because fakes bypass the provider graph, and the UI "worked" because the session state machine is independent of the header plumbing — only a live end-to-end drive crosses both. The bridge is the standard inversion for DI cycles (the dependent registers into a passive seam), keeps `simf_data_pkg` ignorant of the auth package, costs one nullable field, and the regression test pins the contract at the exact layer that failed (the wire), not at the state machine that lied. |

The flag + creds bind through a typed Options section (CLAUDE §18); secrets stay in the out-of-repo env script per OPS-001 §6. `CrudPresentationToggle` CP toolbar button (self-persists, two-way bound); **Profile → "Clear saved layout"** action (client-only `ClearAllAsync`, no API/permission). **Interests pilot:** `InterestForm` → `InterestAddEdit` (now keys off `IsEdit`, not `Initial==null`); new `InterestViewDelete` (read-only `<dl>` + `IsDelete`→Deactivate→`SimfConfirm`); `InterestsList` rewired to one toggle + one `CrudShell` per form-kind; bilingual resx added. **No DB / migration / EF / enum / wire-contract change (D-110 intact); | D-352 | 2026-06-08 | **Security hardening + DRY refactor of the Website & Control Panel BFF/auth surface (no API / schema / enum / wire-contract change).** A strict security review of `SIMF.Web`, then a follow-on DRY pass, shipped as separate bisectable commits on `feature/app-cp-api-split`. **Security:** (1) the typed `SimfAccountClient` (Web) and `SimfAccountClient`/`SimfAdminClient` (CP) registrations were missing the "`Api:BaseUrl` must be configured + HTTPS-outside-Development" guard that `SimfAuthClient` already had — a misconfigured `http://` base in production would have forwarded the visitor/**admin bearer token in cleartext**; consolidated into one dependency-free `SimfApiBaseAddress.Resolve(baseUrl, isDevelopment)` in `SIMF.ApiClient`, called by both hosts' `Program.cs`. (C) the 11 repeated `GetTokenAsync`/401 guards in `AccountEndpoints` collapsed into one group `IEndpointFilter`. **Also:** fixed a stale unit test (`SiteContentMapperTests` asserted an empty sponsor logo; D-348 had made it a placeholder data-URI). **Tests:** added `SimfApiBaseAddressTests` (4) + `SimfAuthSessionTests` validator theories; SIMF.Web.Tests 36/36, SIMF.ApiClient.Tests 39/39, Release build 0/0 (Web + CP); live smoke on an isolated port — landing/login/content-feed 200, unauthenticated `/account/api` 302→login, the public client reached the real API end-to-end, no server-side exceptions. **No DB / migration / EF / enum / wire-contract change (D-110 freeze intact); no new endpoint or permission (reuses existing auth).** | Owner asked for a strict Website security review followed by a DRY pass. The cleartext-token gap existed *because* the base-URL guard was copy-pasted per client and one copy drifted — a single shared resolver makes the drift structurally impossible and (owner-approved) overrides the "two hosts duplicate by design" convention for this infra guard only. Log-then-generic-message is the standard split for an information-disclosure fix; threading cancellation matches the in-project `SiteContentEndpoints` pattern. The DRY changes remove real duplication (11 culture getters, 11 token guards, duplicated validators) at the right altitude — the language switch owning its own target, validators beside `MaskEmail`, an endpoint filter for the cross-cutting auth check — without spawning gratuitous utility classes; the shared-component change is backward-compatible so no call site breaks. Each concern is its own commit and only touched files were staged (concurrent workers were active on the branch). |

| D-350 | 2026-06-08 | **Website landing — stored DOM-XSS hardening of the dynamic renderers (security).** A strict security review of the `/content/site`-fed client renderers found that every dynamic section interpolated **backend-sourced, admin-entered** values (speaker / partner names, session + archive + news titles/descriptions, hall labels, sponsor types) **directly into `innerHTML` with no output encoding** — so a stored `"<img src=x onerror=…>"` in any CP-entered field would execute for **every public visitor** (stored DOM-XSS, public blast radius). **Fix (index.html only):** added one `esc()` HTML-escaper (`& < > " '`) and applied it to every backend value before it enters `innerHTML` across **speakers, partners, sessions, news, the archive timeline (`paintArch`/`renderArchiveYears`) and the per-year archive page**, plus the user-data **attributes** (`img alt`, speaker photo `src`, partner logo `src`). Server-controlled values (the `PlaceholderImage` data-URI in the session/news `url(...)`, the hardcoded `uiStr` labels) are left as-is. **Audited but clean (my C# this wave):** the seeder + `/content/site` proxy take no untrusted input, pass `CancellationToken` through, hold no secrets, and `PartnerLogoPlaceholder` already `Uri.EscapeDataString`-encodes the name into the SVG data-URI (no markup injection). **Verified through the gate (live, :5115):** reload shows **18/18 partner logo data-URIs still render** (their `'` encodes to `&#39;`, decoded back inside the `src` attribute), 8 speakers + portraits, 2 sessions, 4 archive years, the archive page opens with intact Arabic title/summary/place/date, **0 broken images, console clean, no horizontal overflow**. | The landing is public and rendered entirely from admin-managed data; without output encoding a single malicious or compromised admin account (or any earlier injection that lands in those columns) turns the public site into a script-execution vector for every visitor. One uniform `esc()` at the output boundary is the idiomatic minimal fix; hardening the **whole** renderer set — including the pre-existing news + archive-timeline renderers that shared the identical flaw — avoids leaving the same hole half-closed. Encoding at output (not input) keeps the stored data faithful and the bilingual text intact. |

| D-340 | 2026-06-08 | **CP shell (`SimfAppShell`) made responsive on phones (CP UI/UX Tier 3).** Below 768px the layout was forcing a horizontal scrollbar: the 264px side-nav stayed a fixed column and the top-bar control row (language + theme + notification bell + user + sign-out ≈ 432px) overflowed a ~485px viewport by ~137px. Two CSS-only changes in `simf-components.css`, scoped entirely to `.simf-shell*` (the CP shell — the Website never renders these classes, so it is unaffected): (1) **`.simf-shell__content { min-inline-size: 0 }`** so the content flex-column can shrink below its children's intrinsic width and contain a wide page itself — a wide `SimfDataGrid` now scrolls inside its own `.simf-grid__scroll` (columns reachable) instead of pushing the document; (2) a **`@media (max-width: 767px)`** block that lets the **top bar wrap** (`flex-wrap: wrap`, auto height) so the controls drop to a second row rather than overflow — wrapping (not hiding) keeps every control reachable and is locale-proof — and turns the **side nav into an overlay**: closed by default (`display:none`, zero layout, never widens the document) and, when the top-bar toggle sets the existing `--nav-hidden` class, shown as an absolutely-positioned in-viewport panel pinned to the inline-start edge (`inset-inline-start: 0`, so right under RTL / left under LTR) capped to `min(82vw, 280px)`. The toggle is **deliberately inverted vs. desktop** (desktop: open by default, `--nav-hidden` hides; mobile: closed by default, `--nav-hidden` reveals) — one boolean, two viewport-appropriate meanings, handled in CSS so the C# stays a single plain flag (no `SimfAppShell.razor` change). **Verified live** at 390/500/1280px on the CP dashboard + `/admin/halls` grid page and on the Website: at mobile `document.scrollWidth == clientWidth` (no horizontal overflow), the toggle opens/closes the nav overlay, wide grids scroll internally; desktop is byte-for-byte unchanged (264px sidebar, 60px single-row top bar, inline toggle); the Website shows no overflow and `usesShell:false`. CSS-only; no C#/API/schema/contract change. | D-253 Tier 3 called for a responsive off-canvas nav; the live multi-viewport audit showed the real overflow source was the top bar (not only the nav), so the fix addresses both. `min-inline-size:0` is the standard flexbox cure for "a flex child won't shrink below its content and pushes the document"; wrapping the top bar beats hiding controls because nothing becomes unreachable and no translated label can break it; `display:none`-when-closed beats an off-canvas slide because an element parked off-screen can still extend `scrollWidth` (the slide attempt did exactly that in testing), whereas `display:none` is guaranteed zero-layout. Scoping every selector to `.simf-shell*` bounds the blast radius to the CP. |

| D-207 | 2026-05-31 | **Per-page / per-action permission system — enforced in both the API and the Control Panel, configurable by role.** Built the full authorization model the gap report (D-aafe769) flagged as the largest functional gap: a holder of a role sees and reaches only the pages and actions granted to that role, and cannot bypass it in either surface. **Owner-approved design:** assignment is roles-only (a user gets permissions by holding a role; no per-user grants); permissions are resolved from roles once and **baked into the JWT** as multi-valued `perm` claims (no per-request DB lookup); **Administrator = wildcard `*`** (never expanded into individual codes — keeps the token small and the super-admin un-lockout-able). **No schema change and no migration** — the `Permission` + `RolePermission` tables already exist in the D-110 frozen schema, so the catalogue is seeded as data only (additive, freeze-safe). the six pre-catalogue codes (D-148 gate triad, D-168 PR/VIP triad) keep their exact strings + grants; `IdentitySeeder` seeds the whole catalogue idempotently (replacing the 6 hand-written `EnsurePermissionAsync` calls with a loop); doc `SIMF-Permission-Catalogue.md`. **Phase 2a — API infra.** `IPermissionResolver`/`PermissionResolver` (Administrator→`["*"]`, else `IPermissionRepository.GetCodesForRolesAsync` — a `RolePermission⋈Role⋈Permission` join); `JwtTokenService.CreateAccessToken` mints the `perm` claims; all three mint paths thread it (`SignInService`, `SessionService` refresh, `DeviceKeyService`); a `PermissionRequirement` + wildcard-aware `PermissionAuthorizationHandler` + dynamic `PermissionPolicyProvider` (materialises `perm:<code>` on demand, delegates other names to the default provider). **Phase 2b — endpoint sweep.** Replaced the role gate (`AdministratorOnly` / `GatesManage` / `GatesOperate` / `GatesViewOwnReports` / `PublicRelationsAccess`) with the matching `perm:<code>` policy on **~190 admin endpoints across 58 files**, keeping `RequireApprovedAccount` + all rate-limit/upload config; removed the now-redundant trailing `GatesManage` role-policy from the 9 gate endpoints; `DELETE /admin/device-keys/{id}` intentionally stays `AdministratorOnly` (niche admin-only action, no catalogue code). **Phase 3 — CP enforcement.** A CP mirror of the policy spine + a `RequirePermissionAttribute`; `/auth/complete` copies the JWT `perm` claims into the auth cookie; `CpNavigation` items carry a `RequiredPermission` and `CpShellLayout` filters the side menu (hides empty groups; the dashboard + not-built stubs stay ungated); an `AuthorizedAction` component hides action buttons; **49 admin pages** switched `[Authorize(Roles=…)]` → `[RequirePermission(…)]` (`SessionModerationDesk` stays `[Authorize]` — its access is data-scoped per-session at the API). **Phase 4 — config + assignment UI.** `IAdminRoleService.Get/SetPermissionsAsync` (Set diff-applies the role's `RolePermission` rows, validates codes against the catalogue, refuses baseline roles, audits `Role.PermissionsUpdated`) + `GET/PUT /admin/roles/{id}/permissions` (`Roles.View` / `Roles.AssignPermissions`) + client + BFF proxy + `RolePermissionsEditor.razor` (grouped checkboxes, reached from the Roles details modal); `CreateAdminForm`'s single "Grant Administrator" checkbox became a role multi-select (the user→role assignment). **Phase 5 — bypass tests.** `PermissionEnforcementTests` (integration): a role granted only `Sessions.View` gets 200 on `/admin/sessions/list` and **403** on `/admin/themes/list`; Administrator wildcard reaches both; a no-permission admin is 403'd everywhere. `PermissionResolverTests`, `PermissionCatalogTests`, `CpNavigationPermissionTests`. **Bug found + fixed by the new tests:** in `PermissionCatalog` the `AdminOnly`/`GateOperator`/`PublicRelations` baseline lists were declared *after* `All = BuildAll()`, so static-init order captured their null defaults — every `BaselineRoles` came out null, which would NRE the seeder's grant loop at real startup; fixed by ordering the fields before `All`. **Simplify pass:** removed 4 resx keys my own edits orphaned (`Admin.Roles.Details.PermissionEditorDeferred`, `Admin.CreateUser.GrantAdministrator`, EN+AR). **Verification:** full solution builds `-c Release` **0 warnings / 0 errors**; **full suite green in Release — 685 tests, 0 failures** (Api 569, ControlPanel 55, Web 27, ApiClient 13, Application 16, Domain 5; 566→569 = +3 new integration tests, no regression from the 190-endpoint sweep). **Reported, deliberately NOT changed (per §14/§17):** the now-dead `Permissions` constants class + the 4 unused role-based `AuthorizationPolicies` (orphaned by the sweep, in files I didn't author — flagged for an owner-approved cleanup, not deleted unilaterally); Issue-1 widens it to `perm`), so a mid-session grant/revoke isn't reflected in the CP *UI* gates until re-sign-in — **the API always re-checks the fresh JWT, so this is UX/visibility staleness, not an authorization bypass.** | The gap report named the permission system the biggest gap, and the owner approved the shape (roles-only, JWT-baked, Admin=wildcard, sequence gap-report→permissions→E2E) before the build. | D-206 | 2026-05-31 | **Forced password change at first sign-in — in-flow ticket + popup (Control Panel), replacing the dead-end 403 message.** Owner-reported: a seeded/admin-rotated Control Panel credential (flag `PasswordChangeRequired=true`) hit the sign-in 403 `AUTH_PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` with a *"use the password-reset flow"* message and no way forward. Reworked into the standard first-login change flow (AD / Cognito `NEW_PASSWORD_REQUIRED` / Okta "Update Password" pattern), **reusing the codebase's own mid-auth ticket mechanism** rather than inventing an anonymous credential endpoint. **Backend.** `SignInService.SignInAsync` — after the password is verified *and the audience gate passes* (so a wrong-surface caller hits `AUTH_WRONG_SURFACE` first and the branch is not an account-existence oracle; D-080 state-block ordering preserved), a `PasswordChangeRequired` account on the **`Cp` audience** is issued a single-use `SecondFactorToken` of new kind `SecondFactorKind.PasswordChange` (additive enum value — freeze-permitted per D-110; **no schema change**, reuses the existing hashed/TTL/single-use/attempt-capped ticket table) and the response carries it in a new optional `SignInResponse.PasswordChangeToken` field; **every other audience keeps the 403 unchanged** (mobile/web untouched). The forced-change gate still fires at every later token-mint path via `RequirePasswordChangeNotRequired` (verify-totp / verify-recovery / verify-otp / refresh), so no session is minted until the password is actually changed. New `PasswordService.CompletePasswordChangeAsync` (modelled on `ResetPasswordAsync`, authorised by the ticket instead of an emailed code): validates the ticket (kind/consumed/expiry — generic `AUTH_MFA_TOKEN_INVALID/EXPIRED`, no oracle), re-checks the flag, then in one transaction sets the new password (`SetPasswordAsync` — current password NOT re-collected, the ticket already proved it), consumes the ticket, clears the flag, revokes all refresh tokens, audits `PasswordChanged` + dispatches the shared security notice. New anonymous, ticket-gated endpoint `POST /auth/complete-password-change` (mirrors `verify-totp`'s anonymous+ticket posture — **not** a new credential surface) + validator (`StrongPassword` + confirm-match). New audit event `SignIn.PasswordChangeTicketIssued`. **Frontend.** Extracted the Profile change-password form into a shared, endpoint-agnostic `ChangePasswordCard` component (`ShowCurrentField` param + `OnSubmit` callback); **Profile refactored to use it** (no behaviour change), and the `/login` page shows it in a `SimfModal` popup (current-password field hidden — the ticket proves it; only new + confirm) when sign-in returns a `PasswordChangeToken`. On success: no session is minted, the popup closes, the password field clears and a success banner tells the operator to sign in with the new password. New `SimfAuthClient.CompletePasswordChangeAsync` (called directly, like ForgotPassword/ResetPassword — auth pages don't use the cookie BFF); 6 `Auth.ChangePassword.*` resx keys per culture (EN+AR). **Simplify pass:** deduped the password-changed security-notice into a shared `PasswordService.SendPasswordChangedNoticeAsync` used by both the authenticated-change and forced-change paths. **Tests (7 new/updated, all green):** `SignInTests` — old "blocked-403-for-CP" replaced by CP-returns-a-ticket (+ asserts the issued-audit), non-CP-still-403, complete-change-clears-flag-and-lets-sign-in-proceed, unknown-ticket→400; `ChangePasswordCardTests` (bUnit, 3) — current-field shown/hidden by param + OnSubmit payload. **Verification:** full solution `-c Release` = 0/0; full suite **663 green** (Api 566, CP 50, Web 27, ApiClient 13, Domain 5, Application 2). **Does NOT change:** the email-OTP reset flow (kept for genuinely forgotten passwords), the authenticated `/auth/change-password` endpoint, the sign-in 403 contract for non-CP audiences, EF schema (Identity frozen; only an additive enum value). | The owner asked to "open the change-password page instead of showing the message," and the right shape is the industry-standard forced-change-at-first-login: prove possession of the temporary credential, then gate the change on a short-lived single-use challenge — **never mint a session first.** The deciding discovery was that the codebase *already* has this primitive: sign-in returns a short-lived `MfaToken` (a `SecondFactorToken`) and routes to a second step, and `verify-totp` is already `AllowAnonymous` + ticket-authenticated. So the ticket approach is consistent with the codebase (§19) and **avoids a new anonymous credential endpoint** (the alternative — re-posting email+current+new anonymously — would be a genuine §4 exception with a user-enumeration/oracle to defend, and would re-ask the password the user just typed). Authorising the change by the ticket (not a re-typed password) is exactly the owner's "we already have the current password" instinct, done securely — the ticket is the proof. Gating on the `Cp` audience keeps mobile/web on the existing 403, so the blast radius is the Control Panel only. Reusing `SetPasswordAsync` + `ClearChangeFlagAndEndSessionsAsync` (the reset path's mechanics) and extracting `ChangePasswordCard` (one form, two hosts) honours §0 "one clear way" — the new surface is just an entry point + a popup. The additive `SecondFactorKind.PasswordChange` is freeze-safe (D-110 permits appending enum values) and needs no migration because the ticket table already stores `Kind` as an int. The one judgement call (no current-password re-entry) is sound: the ticket is single-use, short-TTL, attempt-capped and issued only after the password verified at sign-in, so re-verifying adds friction without security. |

| D-198 | 2026-05-30 | **Enumeration-resistant sign-up + "complete your profile" sign-in signal.** Owner-requested: re-sign-up must let a user "continue as a fresh one" without ever feeling they already have an account, and a verified-but-profileless user must be routed to the profile form on next login. **Part A — `RegistrationService.SignUpAsync` branches on the existing account's state instead of throwing 409.** Was: any existing email → `409 AUTH_EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (an enumeration oracle, and a dead end for an honest user who forgot an unfinished sign-up). Now three paths, all returning the **same** `SignUpResponse(email, 600)` shape so existence never leaks: **(1) no account** → unchanged create-in-`Registered` + email code; **(2) existing + `Registered` (unverified)** → `RestartUnverifiedAccountAsync`: replace the password with the newly typed one (`RemovePasswordAsync` + `AddPasswordAsync` — `ChangePasswordAsync` needs the old password we don't have), roll the security stamp (H5/D-060), invalidate the old code + issue a fresh one, all inside the existing `transactionRunner` scope so a weak-password `AddPassword` failure rolls back cleanly; the per-account code cap (5/hour, shared with resend) still applies → `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (429); **(3) existing + verified** (`EmailVerified`/`PendingApproval`/`Approved`/`Rejected`/`Disabled`) → `DeflectExistingVerifiedAccountAsync`: the account is **never touched** (password ignored, no code minted), a security heads-up email is sent to the **owner** (sign-in / reset-password), and the same generic 201 is returned. **Part B — `SignInService.BuildAccountStateInfoAsync` now also emits `AccountStateInfo(State="EmailVerified")`** (was null for that state), so the login response tells the client "verified, profile pending" the same way it already signals PendingApproval/Rejected. The `account_state` JWT claim already carries this on every token, so the signal also survives the email-OTP path where the response helper is not reached — the client should treat the claim as the universal signal and the response field as the direct-path convenience mirror. **New audit events** (`AuditEvents`, not the frozen enum): `SignUp.RestartedUnverified` (Success) + `SignUp.ExistingAccountDeflected` (Failure, carries `AUTH_EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` for SOC). `SignIn.AsGuest` now also fires for EmailVerified (comment updated). **Refactor (DRY, serves the feature):** extracted `EnqueueVerificationCodeAsync` + `ToAccountCreationException` shared by the new-account and restart paths; `ResendCodeAsync` left untouched (out of scope, §17). **Docs:** `SIMF-API-001` §12.4 sign-up rewritten (behaviour list; 409 removed from the failure line; the `AUTH_EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED`/409 catalog row stays — still returned by admin-create + walk-in). **Tests (5 added/updated, all 481 Api tests green):** `RegistrationEndpointsTests` — the old `…returns_409…` replaced by `…unverified_account_restarts…` (old code rejected, new code verifies, NEW password signs in + old 401s) + `…verified_account_returns_201_without_revealing_or_touching_it` (state unchanged, 0 codes minted, original password still signs in); `AuditLogTests` — the broken duplicate-audit test split into restart-audit + deflect-audit; `SignInTests` — `…surfaces_EmailVerified`. **What D-198 does NOT change.** No EF schema / no enum change — D-110 freeze intact (reuses `Registered`/`EmailVerified`). The 2FA / email-OTP-every-login question is explicitly **out of scope** and unresolved — see the separate note below. The `AUTH_EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` code itself is retained (admin-create + walk-in still 409). **Foreign uncommitted change observed, not mine, left alone:** `JwtTokenService.cs` had a cosmetic whitespace-only edit in the working tree (no logic), not authored by this change and not committed with it. | The owner's model is "sign-up should never shame or block a returning user, and never confirm an email's existence." That is the textbook OWASP enumeration-resistant sign-up, and it aligns sign-up with this codebase's own sign-in philosophy (one generic response, never an existence oracle — `SignInService` already does this). The verified-account branch is the security crux and was confirmed with the owner before coding: blindly "resend an OTP to continue" for *any* existing account would be account-takeover (a stranger types victim@email + a new password and could seize the account), so the verified branch must touch nothing and notify the owner instead. Replacing the password on the **unverified** branch is safe because an unverified account has no real owner yet — "continue as fresh" means the latest password wins; rolling the security stamp invalidates any token minted against the prior credential. Reusing `transactionRunner` keeps the "user row + code commit together, or not at all" guarantee the original sign-up relied on. Part B leans on the always-present `account_state` claim as the universal signal (works on both the direct and email-OTP sign-in paths) and adds the response mirror only where it's reachable, so it is correct regardless of how the open 2FA question resolves. Kept deliberately out of scope (§17 one-issue-per-change): **the email-OTP-every-login rule.** The owner states visitors must email-OTP at every login; the shipped code makes 2FA opt-in (default off → a fresh verified visitor signs in directly, proven by `SignInTests.SignIn_returns_tokens_directly_when_TwoFactorEnabled_is_false_for_a_visitor`, per D-033/#34). That requirement-vs-code gap is real but is a separate security-flow change (amending D-033) needing its own §11 plan + owner approval — not bundled into this sign-up/profile-signal work. |
| D-197 | 2026-05-30 | **Profile-upsert validation hardening — DOB ≥ 18 + real Luhn ID checksums + passport shape.** Owner-requested real validation on `UpsertUserProfileRequestValidator` (the D-192 review found the ID fields were prefix/length-only and DOB had no rule at all). Three changes, all on `SIMF.Api/Endpoints/Account/Validators/UpsertUserProfileRequestValidator.cs`, with the client mirroring them (§7 validation-alignment). **(1) Date of birth — required + min age 18.** Was: no rule (a null DOB persisted silently). Now: `NotNull` + a `BeAtLeastEighteen` check (`dob <= today.AddYears(-18)`, leap-safe; `DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.UtcNow)` — min-age is not timing-sensitive). **(2) Saudi National ID / Iqama — real Luhn checksum.** Was: prefix+length regex only (`^1\d{9}$` / `^2\d{9}$`).
