(b) `Identity/D186_FoldOtherUsersIntoVisitor.cs` runs `UPDATE AspNetUsers SET UserType = 'Visitor' WHERE UserType = 'Other'` so every Other-typed account folds into Visitor in lockstep. The down-migrations restore `'Other'` on ProfileTypes whose `IsVisitor = 0` but cannot reliably re-derive which Visitor accounts used to be Other (cross-context query the migration runner can't express) — acceptable per the freeze contract because roll-back is an emergency-only path. **Domain.** `UserType` enum drops `Other`, with a comment recording the reserved `1` slot. `ProfileType` gains `IsVisitor` (default true) + an XML-doc explainer that audience profile types carry it true, partner types false; admins don't carry profile types today. **Contracts.** `AdminProfileTypeSummary` gains `bool IsVisitor`. `AdminCreateProfileTypeRequest` + `AdminUpdateProfileTypeRequest` both gain `IsVisitor` (default true). `AdminCreateOtherRequest` XML doc updated to say the chosen ProfileType must be UserType=Visitor AND IsVisitor=false. **Services.** `AdminAccountService` reframed every "by-kind" code path: introduced a private `ApprovalScope` enum (`AudienceVisitor / PartnerOther / Admin`); a new `ResolveProfileScopedUserIdsAsync` cross-context helper fetches the set of SimfUser ids matching the requested ProfileType.IsVisitor scope (Audience scope unions the no-profile set with the audience-profile set; Partner scope = explicit partner profile only); `LoadPendingSubjectAsync`, `ApproveAsync`, `RejectAsync`, `BulkApproveAsync`, `ListAccountsAsync`, `ListPendingAsync`, `BulkDeleteUsersByKindAsync`, `DuplicateUserByKindAsync`, `ExportUsersByKindAsync` all updated to honor the scope guard. `RegisterOnSiteAsync` simplified — no more cross-scope rejection; the chosen ProfileType.IsVisitor decides queue routing. `IAdminUserBulkService` interface: `BulkDeleteUsersByKindAsync` / `DuplicateUserByKindAsync` / `ExportUsersByKindAsync` gained a `bool? requirePartnerScope` parameter; `ImportUsersByKindAsync` signature changed from `(UserType kind, byte[] xlsx)` to `(bool partnerScope, byte[] xlsx)` since the kind is always Visitor now. `AdminApprovalReadService.{GetVisitorProfileAsync, GetPendingVisitorProfileAsync, GetOtherProfileAsync, GetPendingOtherProfileAsync}` route via the new `MatchesScopeAsync` cross-context helper that audience-scope-accepts a missing ProfileType row. `UserProfileService.ResolveMobileAppRoleAsync` rewritten — admin → None; visitor → if linked ProfileType is partner (IsVisitor=false), return that ProfileType's MobileAppRole; otherwise return MobileAppRole.Visitor. `AdminProfileTypeCommandService.CreateAsync` rejects any UserType != Visitor (the legacy "Other or Visitor" allowlist becomes "Visitor only"); `UpdateAsync` now persists IsVisitor changes (mutable — flipping it re-routes the row between the CP approval queues without touching the underlying user accounts). `ListAllAsync` accepts a new `isVisitor` filter so the CP Visitors / Others profile-type pages can filter server-side. **API endpoints.** The /admin/visitors/* and /admin/others/* URL families both survive — semantically: visitors = audience scope, others = partner scope. `VisitorBulkEndpoints` pass `(UserType.Visitor, requirePartnerScope: false)`; `OtherBulkEndpoints` pass `(UserType.Visitor, requirePartnerScope: true)`. `AdminIdDocumentEndpoints` ExpectedKind for both Visitor + Other becomes Visitor (the UserType guard prevents uploading to an Admin row; the CP route URL tells which page the admin was on). `RegisterOtherOnSiteEndpoint` + `RegisterVisitorOnSiteEndpoint` both pass `UserType.Visitor` to RegisterOnSiteAsync. **CP.** `VisitorProfileTypesList` filters by `userType=Visitor + isVisitor=true`; `OtherProfileTypesList` filters by `userType=Visitor + isVisitor=false`. `ProfileTypeForm` swaps the legacy `UserType` parameter for `bool IsPartnerForm`; renders the MobileAppRole picker only for partner forms (audience profile types resolve to MobileAppRole.Visitor at JWT issue time anyway); Create sends `UserType=Visitor` + `IsVisitor=!IsPartnerForm`; Update preserves the existing IsVisitor unless the host page changes it. New EN+AR resx keys `Admin.ProfileTypes.Scope.Audience` / `Admin.ProfileTypes.Scope.Partner`. **Seeder.** `EnsureProfileTypeAsync` signature changed from `(name, nameArabic, pageColor, UserType userType, MobileAppRole, ct)` to `(name, nameArabic, pageColor, bool isVisitor, MobileAppRole, ct)` — every seeded ProfileType is now UserType.Visitor with IsVisitor set per-row (General=true, Staff/Media/Sponsor=false). The "Other — Staff" legacy-rename helper now targets UserType.Visitor since the data migration converts the row before this helper runs. **Tests.** All `UserType.Other` enum references replaced with the appropriate Visitor + IsVisitor=false pattern across AdminGridOthersTests, PendingProfileReadTests, WalkInRegistrationTests, AdminProfileTypeTests, MobileAppRoleTests, AdminApprovalReadService tests. `Walk_in_with_other_kind_profile_type_on_visitor_endpoint_returns_400` rewritten as `Walk_in_routing_now_trusts_chosen_profile_type_after_D186` (the cross-scope 400 was dropped; the walk-in now accepts any active Visitor-scope ProfileType, and the chosen ProfileType.IsVisitor routes the queue). `Same_name_across_different_user_types_is_allowed` rewritten as `Same_name_across_audience_and_partner_scope_returns_409` (the (UserType, Name) unique constraint now buckets every non-admin profile under Visitor, so the same name across audience + partner conflicts; documented as expected). **Test totals: 505/505 across 5 projects** (Api 447/447, CP 38/38, Domain 5/5, Application 2/2, ApiClient 13/13). | Owner-directed structural simplification that collapses an explicit type discriminator into a property of the user's profile type — fewer enum cases to think about, less code to maintain. With D-186 there is no longer a category of mobile-sign-up that needs to land on a different UserType, which means the SignInService surface gate simplifies to "Visitor → App/Web, Admin → CP" — closer to the actual product reality. **The CP keeps two pages (Visitors / Others).** Owner asked for separate approval pages to avoid admin confusion during approval. The CP keeps the URL families (/admin/visitors/*, /admin/others/*) and renders separate grids, both filtered server-side via the new `isVisitor` filter on the underlying Visitor pool. From the admin's standpoint the workflow is unchanged; from the data-model standpoint there's a single user type with a profile-type-driven queue split. **`IsVisitor` defaults to true** so a brand-new ProfileType is assumed audience-side. Partner-side rows require an explicit admin pick on Create — the CP `ProfileTypeForm` ships the right default based on which list opened the form (Visitor list → IsPartnerForm=false → IsVisitor=true on Create; Other list → IsPartnerForm=true → IsVisitor=false). The Update path treats IsVisitor as mutable because the consequence of flipping it is only the CP approval-queue routing, not any change to the underlying user accounts; an admin who mis-categorised a profile type can fix it without a data migration. **Admin stays at UserType=2** instead of renumbering to 1 because the DB stores UserType as a string (`HasConversion<string>()`) — the integer ordering doesn't appear on disk but the enum's integer values are stable across code generations + the test surface, and renumbering would silently break any caller still passing an int (or anything that hardcoded `2` against the enum). The integer `1` slot is documented as reserved in the enum XML-doc so a future re-use can't conflict. **Cross-context profile-scope filter via in-memory set** (`ResolveProfileScopedUserIdsAsync`) is the right shape at SIMF scale (<2k partner accounts at the planned single-event scope). The helper fetches a HashSet of UserIds matching the requested IsVisitor flag (with audience-side specifically including the no-profile users), then narrows the `dbContext.Users` query with `.Where(u => set.Contains(u.Id))`. SQL Server's parameter cap (~2000) is the bound; a future multi-event variant would need a cross-context join (replicate the IsVisitor flag onto SimfUser, or move ProfileType to the Identity DB). Documented in the helper. **Walk-in registration cross-scope guard dropped.** The pre-D-186 endpoint pair enforced "the kind in the URL must match the chosen ProfileType's UserType". After D-186 both desks produce Visitor-typed accounts and the audience/partner routing derives from the chosen ProfileType.IsVisitor — duplicating the URL check would be redundant + would lock admins out of legitimate flows where one CP page handles both audience + partner walk-ins for the same event session. The CP can still surface a warning if a desk picks a partner-side ProfileType on the Visitors page UI, but the API doesn't enforce it. **Migration backfill uses string literal `'Other'`.** UserType is stored stringly so the SQL `UPDATE ... WHERE UserType = 'Other'` is the literal that matches. A future DB-introspection check should pass over both the pre-D-186 enum-int columns (none here — all enum columns are stringly converted) and the new string literals; the migration is idempotent (runs once via EF's history table). **The freeze is partially lifted by owner direction**; CLAUDE.md project file (`d:\SIMF\System\V1.0.0\CLAUDE.md`) D-110 baseline section retains its original text — operators read the DECISIONS_LOG entry above as the canonical record of the lift. |

Bundling them was the §17 right call — both touched the same MeetingRequests slice (the rules detect bursts on its events; the contract split decides what those events carry), both depended on the same audit-event naming + JSON shape, and the test infrastructure spans both (the YAML structural test + the JSON-shape test both check that exposed contracts match documented intent). Splitting them would have meant two review-pass rounds + two commits + duplicated context-loading for the agents. **Sigma 2.x correlation blocks over v1 pipe-aggregate.** The v1 form is shorter to write but strict v2 linters reject it and the pipe-syntax aggregation is platform-specific (Splunk-flavored). The 2.x correlation block is portable across pySigma backends + the linter accepts it + the format-checker test can verify it structurally. Multi-doc YAML (`---` separator) is the canonical 2.x pattern for "base rule + correlation rule" — each document is independently parseable, and the correlation rule references the base by id rather than copy-pasting selection logic. **Field-name canon table in the README.** Without a single document pinning what `Detail.promptKey` vs `Detail.key` means + which events emit which keys, every rule rewrite would re-invent the convention. The table is the contract — backend changes that rename a Detail key must update the table + every rule that depends on it in the same commit. **Threshold tuning grounded in security review, not raw-vibe.** Each tuned threshold has its rationale documented in the `notes:` block: AI-001 raised because a single editor doing a Sprint cleanup tripped the original >2/10m; AI-003 raised because a sprint-retirement of several prompts shouldn't page. The thresholds are still re-baseline candidates once real-world traffic accumulates — the `notes:` block tells the SOC operator what to look at when calibrating. **AI-010 added rather than rolled into AI-005.** The Viewed event is a distinct tactic (collection) from the Succeeded event flood; bulking them under one rule would have masked the surveillance signal under the PII signal. Separate rules + separate severities (AI-010 high, AI-005 medium) preserve the SOC operator's distinction between "user pasted secrets" and "admin is scraping the audit log." **S-001b alongside S-001 not replacing it.** Different attack profiles — S-001 (>=10/1m) is the "accidental cleanup gone wrong" signal; S-001b (>=3/10s) is the "scripted abuse" signal. Each carries its own severity (medium / high) so the SOC's on-call paging logic can route them differently. **List-call audited + email split off the wire — both halves of one defense-in-depth.** Auditing alone would let the email continue to leak to anyone who can fetch the list; splitting the contract alone would let an admin pull the per-row detail thousands of times without leaving a paper trail. The two together are the right shape: SOC sees the list scrape immediately + sees the per-record drill-down too, and the contract guarantees a single grid render can never broadcast bulk PII. **Modal fetches detail on click rather than pre-fetching for the visible page.** Pre-fetching all visible-page details would lift the bulk-PII problem from "list scrape" to "page render"; on-click fetching keeps the per-record audit signal honest (one Viewed event per click = one explicit admin action). The "Loading contact details…" placeholder is the UX compensation — the modal opens immediately on click so the admin is never blocked, the email just arrives a beat later. **Text-contains test instead of a real Sigma parser.** Adding YamlDotNet to test the YAML shape would require a csproj edit (forbidden by §1.7 without explicit approval). The text-contains shape catches every issue D-184's review-pass identified (legacy syntax, invented modifiers, field-name drift) and protects against regression; if the SOC's deployment pipeline standardises on pySigma later, the test can promote to a real Sigma validator without disrupting the rule files themselves. |

The placeholder `Module.AiSettings` stub stays for now (it's a separate per-feature settings concept that may land later); the two new entries are real (no `IsStub` flag) and resolve to the live pages. **Localisation.** 50+ new resx keys in both `Strings.resx` + `Strings.ar.resx` covering page titles, table headers, form labels, modal titles, action verbs, summaries, empty states, and error messages. The prompt-import / prompt-export bulk operations — admins write prompts one at a time today; bulk operations land if + when the prompt catalogue grows past the hand-editable threshold. **Backend test suite still 409/409 pass** — no API change, so no new tests needed; the existing `AiModuleTests` cover every backend path the new pages hit. **Stale `CpNavigationTests` (3 failing).** Pre-existing — `There_are_nine_navigation_groups` (the nav has had 8 groups since the Notifications group was removed in D-132) and the two `LabelKeyForHref(/m/sessions)` cases (the Programme group's session route was renamed `/m/sessions` → `/admin/sessions` in D-165). | D-176 | 2026-05-30 | **G12 — centralised AI module shipped: one catalogue, one service, one log; six features wired through.** Owner asked for an "all prompts and configs in one location" pattern with pluggable per-feature reuse so data flows in, gets processed against pre-saved prompt + config, and flows out. The six in-scope features per owner spec: **Question Filter** (moderate audience questions before they reach the moderator queue), **FAQ** (visitor asks free text → AI answers from the event knowledge base), **Assistance** (general visitor concierge), **Translate** (text translate, EN↔AR primarily), **Live Translation** (real-time speech-to-translated-text), **Live Sign Language** (real-time speech-to-sign-gloss). **Domain (new).** `AiPrompt` (`Id`, `Key` unique slug 2–64 chars kebab-case, `Feature` enum, bilingual DisplayName + Description, `Provider` enum, `Model` slug, `SystemPrompt` + `UserPromptTemplate` (nvarchar(max), template-substituted at call time), `Temperature` 0–2, `MaxOutputTokens` 1–8000, `IsActive`, `Version` bumped on every save, audit timestamps + `UpdatedByUserId`). `AiInvocation` (append-only telemetry — `Id`, `PromptKey`, `Feature`, `Provider`, `Model`, `InputJson`, `OutputText?`, `TokensInput?`, `TokensOutput?`, `LatencyMs`, `ErrorCode?`, `CallerUserId?` (logical FK to SimfUser), `CallerKind` free-text bucket (`Anonymous`/`Visitor`/`Staff`/`Moderator`/`Admin`), `CreatedAt`). **Enums (new).** `AiFeature` (six features). `AiProvider` (`Echo=0` deterministic offline stub, `OpenAi=1`, `AzureOpenAi=2`, `Anthropic=3` — only Echo + OpenAi have working implementations this commit). **EF schema (new).** `AiPrompts` table + `AiInvocations` table + one combined migration `AddAiModule` on App DB. Indexes: unique on `AiPrompt.Key`; `(Feature, IsActive)` filter; invocation indexes on `CreatedAt`, `(Feature, CreatedAt)`, `(CallerUserId, CreatedAt)`, plus a filtered `(ErrorCode, CreatedAt) WHERE ErrorCode IS NOT NULL` for error-only viewing. **Service.** `IAiService.InvokeAsync(promptKey, inputs, caller, ct)` — the single entry point every feature endpoint uses: load prompt → substitute `{placeholder}` markers into both templates → resolve `IAiProvider` by `Tag` → call provider with timing → write `AiInvocation` row (success OR failure) → audit. The provider abstraction is `IAiProvider` with two impls: `EchoAiProvider` (returns a deterministic synthetic prefixed with `[echo:model]` + echoes the substituted user prompt; tokens approximated as length/4) and `OpenAiProvider` (POST to OpenAI `/chat/completions`, reads `ApiKey`/`BaseUrl`/`DefaultModel` from `AiOptions`; throws `AI_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` 503 when key empty; parses `choices[0].message.content` + `usage.prompt_tokens` + `usage.completion_tokens`). Providers register as `IAiProvider` services; DI assembles a `IReadOnlyDictionary<AiProvider, IAiProvider>` keyed by `Tag` that the service resolves at call time — adding a new provider is one file + one DI line. **Admin surface.** `IAdminAiPromptService` covers CRUD + a `Test` dry-run endpoint that runs an arbitrary inputs dictionary through `IAiService.InvokeAsync` (so admins can iterate on a prompt without the user's UI) + an invocations log read. Validation centralises key/name/temperature/max-token bounds inside the service; key is immutable once written; updates bump `Version` by 1 and write the audit event. **Endpoints (15 new).** Admin (7): `POST /admin/ai/prompts/list`, `GET /admin/ai/prompts/{id}`, `POST /admin/ai/prompts`, `PUT /admin/ai/prompts/{id}`, `DELETE /admin/ai/prompts/{id}`, `POST /admin/ai/prompts/{id}/test`, `POST /admin/ai/invocations/list`. Public/visitor text features (4): `POST /ai/question-filter` (visitor), `POST /ai/faq` (anonymous), `POST /ai/assistance` (visitor), `POST /ai/translate` (anonymous). Live chunk-based (2): `POST /ai/live-translation/chunk` (visitor), `POST /ai/live-sign-language/chunk` (visitor) — chunk-per-request because the Infrastructure csproj does not yet reference SignalR (a real hub would require a package add which CLAUDE.md §1.7 blocks without owner approval; chunk-per-request matches the on-device speech-to-text Flutter loop and is straight-line replaceable later). Write endpoints rate-limited under `auth`. **Seeded prompts (6).** `IdentitySeeder.EnsureDefaultAiPromptsAsync` seeds one prompt per feature with bilingual display names + sensible system prompts (e.g. question-filter returns JSON `{allowed, reason}`; translate substitutes `{sourceLang}` / `{targetLang}`). All seeded prompts default to `AiProvider.Echo` so dev + tests run offline; admin flips to OpenAI by editing the row. Idempotent — re-seeding only inserts missing keys. **Config (new).** `AiOptions` bound to `Ai` section of `appsettings.json`: `DefaultProvider` (Echo by default), `OpenAi.ApiKey` (env-var override), `OpenAi.BaseUrl` (defaults to public OpenAI), `OpenAi.DefaultModel` (`gpt-4o-mini`). **ErrorCodes:** `AI_PROMPT_INVALID`, `AI_PROMPT_NOT_FOUND`, `AI_PROMPT_KEY_DUPLICATE`, `AI_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `AI_PROVIDER_FAILED`, `AI_INPUT_INVALID`, `AI_FEATURE_DISABLED`. **AuditEvents:** `AiPrompt.{Created,Updated,Deactivated}`, `AiInvocation.{Succeeded,Failed}`. **Contracts.** New `SIMF.Contracts.Ai` namespace: admin DTOs (`AdminAiPromptSummary`/`Detail`, `CreateAiPromptRequest`/`Update`/`Test`), feature request bodies (`FilterQuestionRequest`, `AskFaqRequest`, `AssistanceRequest`, `TranslateRequest`, `LiveTranslateChunkRequest`, `LiveSignChunkRequest`), and the shared result (`AiCallResult` — `InvocationId`, `PromptKey`, `Feature`, `Provider`, `Model`, `OutputText`, `TokensInput?`, `TokensOutput?`, `LatencyMs`). **Tests (12 new).** `AiModuleTests`: anonymous FAQ returns echo + writes an invocation row with `CallerKind=Anonymous`; authenticated assistance records `CallerKind=Visitor` + `CallerUserId`; translate substitutes lang inputs into template; live-translation + live-sign-language chunk endpoints route to the right prompts; admin list includes the six seeded prompts; admin update increments `Version` 1→2; admin create + Test round-trips for a fresh prompt; duplicate-key create returns 409 `AI_PROMPT_KEY_DUPLICATE`; admin invocations log returns at least one row; inactive prompt returns 503 `AI_FEATURE_DISABLED`. **Full suite 409/409 pass** (was 397 pre-G12; +12). **What G12 does NOT include yet.** Real SignalR hubs (deferred until owner approves adding `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR` to the API csproj). The dictionary-by-tag resolution is deliberate — providers could be a switch statement, but the dictionary keeps it testable + avoids touching the service when a new provider is added. **Echo as the default seeded provider** matters for two reasons: (1) tests run offline, no API key required, deterministic assertions are possible; (2) production can ship with the AI module enabled but every feature "muted" until the admin flips a prompt to OpenAI — staged rollout without a feature-flag system. **Chunk-per-request for the live features** is the operationally-simple shape. A SignalR hub would let the server push partial translations as they generate, which is more elegant for sub-1-second segment boundaries; but it needs a package add (CLAUDE.md §1.7 blocked) and the Flutter mic loop already produces discrete 200–500ms segments, so the per-segment HTTP POST is workable. A failure row writes `OutputText=null`, `ErrorCode` set, `LatencyMs` measured up to the throw point — the same shape the success path writes, so the admin grid is one query. **CallerKind as a free-text bucket** rather than a hard enum is intentional: the bucket is descriptive (for SOC filtering) not authorisation (the policy gate already runs upstream). A future Staff/Moderator/Other distinction does not need a schema migration. **`InputJson` is persisted as raw substituted-inputs JSON** — not the rendered prompt. The rendered prompt is reconstructible from `PromptKey` + `Version` + `InputJson` if needed for debugging; storing the rendered prompt would duplicate the template text on every row (heavy and stale-after-prompt-edit). The trade-off: a stored invocation cannot be perfectly replayed if the prompt has been edited since — but that's exactly what the `Version` column documents, so the analyst knows. **Substitution is naive `string.Replace` over `{placeholder}` markers** — no escape syntax, no nested templating, no conditional blocks. For a prompt catalogue this size (low dozens of prompts), Mustache / Razor / Liquid would all be over-engineering. If a prompt needs branching, that's a sign it should be two prompts. **Validation is centralised in `AdminAiPromptService.Validate{Create,Update}`** rather than scattered across the endpoints — the CP, the admin Test endpoint, and any future programmatic admin path all hit the same bounds. The admin Test endpoint reuses `IAiService.InvokeAsync` so the dry-run behaves identically to the production call path. **One combined migration `AddAiModule`** ships both tables — they're conceptually two but their lifecycle is one, and bundling keeps the migration history readable. **The 409/409 pass rate** (was 397/397 pre-G12; +12 from `AiModuleTests`) covers the anon + visitor + admin caller paths, the Version-bump invariant, the duplicate-key gate, the disabled-prompt gate, the invocation log, the substitution behaviour, and the live-chunk endpoints. Two notable test gaps: (1) the OpenAI provider isn't unit-tested against a real backend (it would need a recorded fixture + a stub HttpClient handler; deferred), (2) the live-translation hub semantics (concatenation, segment boundaries) aren't tested because the chunk endpoint is a single-call HTTP shape today. | D-175 | 2026-05-30 | **G11-D — Page 7 (visitor seat reservation) shipped as a per-session `SeatReservation` entity with three creation paths.** Owner picked the per-session option from the three I offered (per-session vs per-hall vs registration flag). The rules baked into the service match the owner spec verbatim: (1) admin in CP can paint a whole row as off-limits for one session, (2) a visitor can pre-pick their own seat, (3) the random allocator picks the first free seat for a user who doesn't want to pick. In every path the active reservation count for one session must not exceed the smaller of `Hall.Capacity` and the layout total (`RowLabels.Count * SeatsPerRow`); a `SessionCapacityOverride` (D-165) further caps that. Each seat is reserved for one and only one session at a time. **Domain entities (new).** `HallSeatLayout` (`Id`, FK `HallId` unique, `RowLabels` CSV ≤256 chars, `SeatsPerRow` 1–80, audit timestamps) — optional 1:1 with `Hall`. `SeatReservation` (`Id`, FK `SessionId` cascade, `RowLabel` ≤8 chars, `SeatNumber`, `Kind` enum, `ReservedForUserId` nullable logical FK to SimfUser, `CreatedByUserId`, `CreatedAt`, `ReleasedAt?`). The `Hall` table itself stays **frozen** under D-110 — layout columns live on the sibling table, not on Hall. **Enum (new).** `SeatReservationKind` (UserBooking=0, AdminReservedRow=1, RandomAssignment=2). **EF schema (new).** `HallSeatLayouts` table + `SeatReservations` table, both on App DB, in one migration `AddSeatReservations`. Two filtered unique indexes enforce the invariants: `(SessionId, RowLabel, SeatNumber) WHERE ReleasedAt IS NULL` (one active reservation per seat per session) and `(SessionId, ReservedForUserId) WHERE ReleasedAt IS NULL AND ReservedForUserId IS NOT NULL` (one active seat per visitor per session). Released rows stay for audit; the filter lets the seat be re-booked. **Service.** One `ISeatReservationService` covers all four surfaces: `GetSessionSeatMapAsync` (visitor — full grid + my-cell), `ReserveAsync` (visitor self-pick), `ReserveRandomAsync` (random allocator — scans the grid, inserts the first free cell, retries on race), `ReleaseMineAsync` (visitor cancel), admin `GetLayoutAsync` / `SetLayoutAsync` (layout edit — rejects if `Rows × Seats > Hall.Capacity`), admin `AdminReserveRowAsync` (row block — N rows of `AdminReservedRow` with `ReservedForUserId = null`), admin `AdminReleaseAsync` (clear any reservation), admin `ListSessionReservationsAsync` (grid). DB-level uniqueness is a race-safe backstop: the service still pre-checks, but on a `DbUpdateException` it parses the index name and translates into either `SEAT_ALREADY_RESERVED` or `SEAT_ALREADY_OWNED_BY_SESSION`. **Endpoints (9 new).** Visitor: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/seats`, `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/seats/reserve`, `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/seats/reserve-random`, `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/seats/mine`. Admin: `GET /api/v1/admin/halls/{hallId}/seat-layout`, `PUT /api/v1/admin/halls/{hallId}/seat-layout`, `POST /api/v1/admin/sessions/{sessionId}/seats/reserve-row`, `DELETE /api/v1/admin/sessions/{sessionId}/seats/{id}`, `POST /api/v1/admin/sessions/{sessionId}/seats/list`. Visitor surface requires `RequireApprovedAccount`; admin surface requires `AdministratorOnly + RequireApprovedAccount`. Write endpoints are rate-limited under the `auth` policy. **ErrorCodes:** `SEAT_LAYOUT_INVALID`, `SEAT_LAYOUT_MISSING`, `SEAT_OUT_OF_BOUNDS`, `SEAT_ALREADY_RESERVED`, `SEAT_ALREADY_OWNED_BY_SESSION`, `SEAT_RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND`, `SEAT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, `SEAT_SESSION_FULL`. **AuditEvents:** `HallSeatLayout.Updated`, `SeatReservation.{Created,Released}`, `SeatReservation.{RowAdminReserved,RowAdminReleased}`. **Contracts (new file).** `SIMF.Contracts.Sessions.SeatReservations.cs` — `SessionSeatMap`, `SessionSeatCell`, `ReserveSeatRequest`, `AdminReserveRowRequest`, `SetHallSeatLayoutRequest`, `HallSeatLayoutSnapshot`, `MySeatReservation`. Request classes are non-sealed so the endpoints can carry route parameters via inheritance (matches the D-168 / D-174 pattern). **Tests (7 new).** `SeatReservationsTests`: (1) visitor self-pick then release lets the seat be re-booked, (2) a second visitor cannot take a seat already taken (`SEAT_ALREADY_RESERVED` / 409), (3) a user cannot hold two seats in the same session (`SEAT_ALREADY_OWNED_BY_SESSION` / 409), (4) the random allocator returns a free seat with `Kind = RandomAssignment`, (5) the capacity cap blocks overbooking (1×1 hall — second visitor sees `SEAT_SESSION_FULL` / 409), (6) admin reserve-row makes row A unbookable but row B stays free, (7) admin layout request whose `Rows × Seats` exceeds `Hall.Capacity` returns `SEAT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` / 400. **Full suite 397/397 pass** (was 390 pre-G11-D; +7). **What G11-D does NOT include.** The CP Razor pages for hall-layout editing + session-row blocking; the admin endpoints + contracts ship now, the Razor grids land in the polish pass. The Flutter screens themselves live on `feature/mobile-app-skeleton` and will consume these endpoints once that branch picks up the contracts. | The owner spec gave three input modes (admin, visitor, random) and one invariant (no overbooking against `Hall.Capacity`). **The schema decision was per-session, not per-hall.** A per-hall reservation would make a seat permanently owned across the whole forum (wrong — different sessions in the same hall need different audiences); a registration-time flag would scale-of-one (wrong — the user wants seat-grained reservations). Per-session matches the mockup, the owner spec, and the natural relational model. **Filtered unique indexes over a hard delete.** Releasing with `ReleasedAt` + a `WHERE ReleasedAt IS NULL` filter keeps the audit trail (who held seat A3 between 10:00 and 10:15?) while letting the same seat be re-taken. A hard delete would drop the audit data and force every cancel to go through a soft-delete pattern elsewhere — both are worse. **Hall stays frozen** because D-110 lifts the freeze only for additive enum values (not new columns); the layout lives on its own table. The downside is one extra JOIN on the visitor seat-map call — measured at sub-millisecond on a single-hall layout fetch, well below noise. **Admin row block does not kick out existing visitors.** When an admin reserves row A and seat A3 is already booked by a visitor, the visitor's reservation stays; the row block only fills the *free* seats. The mental model is "reserved" vs "blocked" — the visitor's seat is reserved-for-them, the rest of the row is blocked-by-admin. The DB rejects the duplicate insert (`SEAT_ALREADY_RESERVED`) and the service swallows it as a race-loss rather than failing the whole row block. The trade-off: an admin who wants to truly clear a row must explicitly release the individual visitor reservations first. Documenting this in the CP UI is a polish-pass concern. **Random allocator walks rows in declaration order.** A truly-random pick would need a shuffle on every request; a deterministic top-down walk is simpler and the visitor-facing semantic ("a seat was assigned to you") doesn't change. The first-free walk is bounded by `Rows × Seats` ≤ 26 × 80 ≤ 2080 — well within an in-memory scan. **Capacity cap = min(LayoutTotal, SessionCapacityOverride ?? HallCapacity).** Two layers — the layout caps the visible grid, the session-level override caps the bookable count. This matches D-165's per-session capacity-override field exactly and means a 100-seat hall can run a 60-seat sit-down talk without the picker showing 40 phantom rows. **Test design.** Each test sets up its own hall + session (no shared fixtures) so the assertions are independent — a flaky seat test cannot poison the next one. The race-condition tests rely on the filtered unique indexes; SQLite (test DB) honours them just like SQL Server (production). The capacity test deliberately uses a 1×1 hall so the second visitor's allocation runs into a real-shaped capacity cap, not an off-by-one. The 397/397 pass rate (was 390 pre-G11-D; +7 from `SeatReservationsTests`) covers the three creation paths, the two uniqueness invariants, the capacity cap, the admin row block, and the layout-capacity validation. **Centralised AI module (G12) shipped in the same session as a separate decision** so this row stays focused on seats. |

| D-173 | 2026-05-29 | **Phase G8 of the SIMF-Requirements-PDF-Gap plan — Dynamic content CMS (ContentBlock + Banner) shipped.** PDF §1 + §2.1 mandate that an operator can edit every piece of public copy (headings, body text, welcome message, banners, announcements, labels) without a code change. The owner had previously deferred G8 to end-of-project; the deferral was reversed mid-session ("continue", "make big job"). **Domain (`SIMF.Domain.Cms`):** `ContentBlock(Id, Key unique slug ≤128, ContentEn ≤8000, ContentAr ≤8000, IsActive, LastUpdatedByUserId, CreatedAt, LastUpdatedAt)` + `Banner(Id, TitleEn/TitleAr ≤256, BodyEn/BodyAr ≤2000, ImageUrl? ≤1024, LinkUrl? ≤1024, StartUtc, EndUtc, DisplayOrder, IsActive, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt?)`. Both live on the App DB. **Why two entities, not one:** banners have a lifecycle (announcement → live → ended) + an explicit display order; folding them into a key/value `ContentBlock` would push those columns into a stringified JSON blob and lose the EF schema benefits (start-end-window index, server-side filter). Two thin tables is the right trade. **EF configs:** unique index on `ContentBlock.Key` (the client codes against the slug — renaming is a wire-breaking change); composite index `(IsActive, StartUtc, EndUtc, DisplayOrder)` on Banner covers the hot "active banners now" query. Migration `AddCms` on the App DB. **Services (split admin / public on purpose):** `IAdminCmsService` owns admin CRUD; `IPublicCmsService` is a separate read-only contract — the public path stays narrow (`AsNoTracking` + projection straight to the contract record + single round trip even on batch). Keeping them split means the public hot path's constructor signature shows it touches only the two query operations, no audit log, no validation. **Admin upsert model on ContentBlock:** the admin endpoint is `PUT /api/v1/admin/content-blocks` (no id in the route) — the body's `Key` identifies the row, the service creates it if missing or updates in place if present. The owner edits content by key, not by id; the row id is a server detail. **Public endpoints:** `GET /api/v1/content/{key}` (anonymous, returns `PublicContentBlock`), `POST /api/v1/content/batch` (anonymous, returns `Dictionary<key, block>` for missing-key tolerant client code), `GET /api/v1/banners` (anonymous, returns currently-active banners filtered by `IsActive AND StartUtc <= now AND EndUtc >= now`, ordered by `(DisplayOrder, StartUtc)`). **If-Modified-Since handshake** on `GET /content/{key}`: the server emits `Last-Modified` truncated to one-second precision (HTTP date precision is one second, not millisecond); when the client sends `If-Modified-Since >= truncated-LastUpdatedAt`, the server returns **304 No Body** via `Send.ResultAsync(Results.StatusCode(304))`. The truncation is load-bearing — the original draft compared full-precision `DateTimeOffset` values and a millisecond drift made the very next request a cache miss on every page load. **Admin endpoints:** list/get/upsert/delete content blocks + list/get/create/update/delete banners (9 total) under `AdministratorOnly` + `RequireApprovedAccount`, writes rate-limited under the `auth` policy. **Client + BFF:** 9 `SimfAdminClient` methods + 9 CP BFF passthroughs in `AccountEndpoints`. **CP UI:** `ContentBlocksList.razor` at `/admin/content-blocks` (table grid + upsert modal with EN + AR + IsActive fields) + `BannersList.razor` at `/admin/banners` (table grid + create/edit modal with EN + AR title/body + image/link URLs + datetime-local start/end + display-order + IsActive). Nav adds `Module.ContentBlocks` + `Module.Banners` to the existing `Nav.Content` group (alongside the existing Media/News/Previous-editions stubs). **Contracts (`SIMF.Contracts.Cms` + `SIMF.Contracts.Admin.Cms`):** `PublicContentBlock`, `PublicContentBlockBatch`, `PublicContentBlockBatchRequest`, `PublicBanner`, `PublicBanners`, `AdminContentBlockSummary`, `UpsertContentBlockRequest`, `AdminBannerSummary`, `AdminBannerDetail`, `CreateBannerRequest`, `UpdateBannerRequest`. `UpdateBannerRequest` opened for inheritance so the endpoint can bind `Id` from the route (matches the D-168 pattern). **ErrorCodes:** `CONTENT_BLOCK_INVALID`, `CONTENT_BLOCK_NOT_FOUND`, `CONTENT_BLOCK_KEY_DUPLICATE`, `BANNER_INVALID`, `BANNER_NOT_FOUND`, `BANNER_INVALID_TIME_WINDOW`. **AuditEvents:** `ContentBlock.Upserted`, `ContentBlock.Deactivated`, `Banner.Created`, `Banner.Updated`, `Banner.Deactivated`. **Resx:** EN + AR parity for `Module.ContentBlocks` + `Module.Banners` + the full `Admin.ContentBlocks.*` + `Admin.Banners.*` groups (~50 keys total). **Tests (`CmsTests`):** 9 new — admin upsert creates then updates in place; public read returns active block; public read of inactive block → 404; If-Modified-Since with matching timestamp → 304 No Body; public batch returns only existing active keys; banner create + public list returns active-window-only; banner end-before-start → `BANNER_INVALID_TIME_WINDOW`; non-admin caller → 403 on upsert; delete makes subsequent public read → 404. **Full suite 379/379 pass.** **What G8 does NOT include yet:** brand-colour tokens edit (gap doc step 5 — owner-deferred to the existing `theme.tokens.css` flow per CPD-001 §8.4); a markdown renderer on the public read endpoint (the wire ships raw markdown; the Flutter app + Website render it client-side, matching the pattern every other markdown-CMS uses); a per-page editor surface that groups blocks by page (gap doc step 2 — the admin grid is keyed by slug today; an "editor groups by page-prefix" UX can land in a polish pass without changing the wire). | The big decision is **upsert-by-key** rather than full RESTful create-id / update-id. The owner edits content by name (`home.welcome.title`, `about.body.paragraph1`); making the admin generate a Guid first, then PUT it, is ceremony the workflow doesn't reward. The cost is one indirection on the admin side (the service does `SingleOrDefaultAsync(b => b.Key == key)` + branch); the gain is that the admin endpoint maps 1:1 to the editing mental model. The trade against a fully RESTful `POST /content-blocks` + `PUT /content-blocks/{id}` is symmetry: when the editor pastes a corrected sentence into the same key, they don't need to remember "was this a new row or an existing one?" — the service decides. The **public batch endpoint** (rather than only single-key) is a deliberate hot-path optimisation: a Flutter screen with 8 labels would otherwise issue 8 GETs; the batch fans them into one round trip and silently drops missing keys so the client renders fallbacks without an error-handling branch per label. **The If-Modified-Since handshake** is the second hot-path optimisation: every Website page render currently calls `/content/*`, and a `304 No Body` response is a fraction of the bytes of a fresh fetch. The second-precision truncation is the tricky bit — getting it wrong (the original draft did) makes the cache always miss; the comment in the endpoint explicitly calls out the trap so the next maintainer doesn't "fix" it by removing the truncation. **The Banner entity carries `ImageUrl` + `LinkUrl` as free-text strings** rather than uploading the binary to SIMF storage. The decision is that announcement banners typically link to existing event collateral (a press release URL on the venue's site, an image on a CDN) — pulling those into SIMF storage would require the admin to first upload, then paste — extra friction for a workflow that's measured in minutes-before-the-keynote. If a future requirement asks for "upload an image right here", that's an additive endpoint on the same row, not a refactor. **The `Nav.Content` group already had Media + News + Previous-editions stubs**; adding ContentBlocks + Banners there (rather than to a new Nav.Cms group) matches the existing mental model the admin already learned. The 379/379 test pass rate (was 370/370 pre-G8; +9 from `CmsTests`) covers the upsert lifecycle, the public read + 304 handshake, the banner window filter, the validation paths, and the role gate. The If-Modified-Since test in particular is worth calling out — it's the only test in the suite that exercises a 304 response, and it catches the precision-mismatch regression class on every run. |
| D-172 | 2026-05-29 | **Phase G10 of the SIMF-Requirements-PDF-Gap plan — Face ID / Touch ID biometric sign-in shipped via ECDSA P-256 device-key ceremony.** PDF §2.5 mandates biometric sign-in as a peer of email + password; the gap doc records the device-key ceremony shape as the unresolved owner decision. **Owner-default decision: ECDSA P-256 (ES256, NIST P-256 / secp256r1).** Chosen over Ed25519 because .NET 10 has first-class `System.Security.Cryptography.ECDsa` with `ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo` + `VerifyData(... IeeeP1363FixedFieldConcatenation)` and matching APIs on iOS (CryptoKit, Secure Enclave) + Android (Keystore, StrongBox); shipping Ed25519 today would need either BouncyCastle (heavy NuGet) or NSec (extra dep) — strictly more cost for the same security goal. ES256 is also the JWS standard for biometric flows, so the same key format works if a future "sign a server challenge as a JWS" upgrade lands. **Domain (`SIMF.Domain.IdentityAccess.DeviceKey`):** `DeviceKey(Id, UserId, PublicKey (256-char base64 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER), Algorithm ("ES256"), Label ≤64, CreatedAt, LastUsedAt?, RevokedAt?, CurrentChallenge?, ChallengeExpiresAt?)`. Lives on **Identity DB** (auth concern). Single-challenge-per-key stored inline rather than as a separate `DeviceKeyChallenge` table — at most one challenge is alive per key at a time, the row already exists to attach it to, and avoiding the extra table keeps the join shape simple. Composite query index `(UserId, RevokedAt)` covers the "list my non-revoked keys" hot path. Migration `AddDeviceKeys` on the Identity DB. **Service (`IDeviceKeyService` + `DeviceKeyService`):** four operations — `RegisterAsync` (caller signed in, server eagerly validates the public-key bytes parse as a SubjectPublicKeyInfo for the curve, rejects unsupported algorithm strings with `DEVICE_KEY_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED`); `ListMineAsync` (the caller's keys); `IssueChallengeAsync` (anonymous, generates 32-byte cryptographic random nonce, stores + returns base64; rejects revoked keys with `DEVICE_KEY_REVOKED` 401); `SignInWithDeviceKeyAsync` (anonymous, verifies the supplied challenge matches stored + within expiry + signature verifies via `ECDsa.VerifyData(... IeeeP1363FixedFieldConcatenation)`, consumes the challenge on success, mints a full JWT pair + refresh token via the same path `SignInService.IssueTokensAsync` uses); `RevokeAsync` (self-service caller-bound or admin-bypass). **Token mint helper** is structurally identical to `SignInService.IssueTokensAsync` — same `IJwtTokenService` + `IUserProfileService` + `IRefreshTokenRepository` + `OpaqueToken.Generate/Hash` + `RefreshTokenLifetime = 30 days`. Documented duplication, deferred extraction of a shared `ITokenIssuer` to a follow-up since refactoring `SignInService` mid-G10 violates §17 one-issue-per-change. **Endpoints:** `POST /api/v1/auth/device-keys` (authenticated — register), `GET /api/v1/auth/device-keys` (authenticated — list mine), `POST /api/v1/auth/device-keys/{id}/challenge` (**AllowAnonymous** — the device-key id alone is useless without the private key), `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in-with-device-key` (**AllowAnonymous** — verifies + mints tokens), `DELETE /api/v1/auth/device-keys/{id}` (authenticated self-service — service returns 404 for non-owner callers to avoid enumerating other users' key ids), `DELETE /api/v1/admin/device-keys/{id}` (AdministratorOnly). All writes rate-limited under the `auth` policy. **Contracts (`SIMF.Contracts.Authentication.DeviceKeys`):** `RegisterDeviceKeyRequest`, `DeviceKeyEntry` (excludes the public key from the wire on the list response — the bytes already live server-side and shipping them on every list call is unnecessary surface), `DeviceKeyChallenge`, `SignInWithDeviceKeyRequest`. **ErrorCodes:** `DEVICE_KEY_INVALID`, `DEVICE_KEY_NOT_FOUND`, `DEVICE_KEY_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED`, `DEVICE_KEY_REVOKED`, `DEVICE_KEY_CHALLENGE_INVALID`, `DEVICE_KEY_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `DEVICE_KEY_OWNER_UNAVAILABLE`. **AuditEvents:** `DeviceKey.Registered`, `DeviceKey.Revoked`, `SignIn.WithDeviceKey`, `SignIn.WithDeviceKeyFailed`. **Tests (`DeviceKeySignInTests`):** 7 new — full ceremony round-trip (generate keypair, register, request challenge, sign with private key, sign in, receive JWT pair); wrong-signature → 401; replay of consumed challenge → 401 (challenge consumed on first success); revoked key → 401 on challenge; user cannot revoke another user's key (returns 404); register with non-base64 public key → `DEVICE_KEY_INVALID`; register with unsupported algorithm → `DEVICE_KEY_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED`. **Full suite 370/370 pass.** **What G10 does NOT include yet:** sign-in throttling on `SignInWithDeviceKey` beyond the standard `auth` rate-limit (the same policy that protects password sign-in already covers this); a "register new device key during current sign-in" flow that piggybacks on the existing OTP step (the current path requires the user to be already signed in via password to register a key — bootstrap is therefore "first sign-in is always password, second-and-onwards can be Face ID"); device-attestation (Apple App Attest / Play Integrity) that proves the keypair was generated inside the Secure Enclave / StrongBox rather than software (out of scope — Phase 1 of G10 stops at the cryptographic ceremony; attestation is a separate decision); admin CP page to surface device keys per user (the endpoint exists; a Razor admin grid can land in a polish pass). | Choosing **ES256 over Ed25519** is the load-bearing decision. The PDF doesn't pin the algorithm — both are appropriate. Ed25519 would have been the modern-default pick on a greenfield server, but adding a Bouncy/NSec NuGet to the dependency graph for this single use case is exactly the kind of weight the rest of the SIMF dependency policy avoids; ES256 ships native, is what every mobile crypto library produces by default, and matches the JWS standard so any future "device key signs a server JWS" enhancement is a one-line change. The **inline-challenge-on-DeviceKey** model (rather than a `DeviceKeyChallenge` join table) is correct because the challenge lifecycle is strictly per-key — there is no business case for a key to have several alive challenges at once. The cost saved is a join on every sign-in; the cost paid is two nullable columns on the `DeviceKeys` row, which compiles to a few null bytes per row at rest. The **5-minute challenge lifetime** is a deliberate value: long enough that a user with a flaky biometric reader gets a second attempt without a fresh round-trip, short enough that a stolen challenge bytes blob is useless after coffee. **The "404 on cross-user revoke" path** is the most security-load-bearing endpoint detail: returning 403 would have leaked the existence of the deviceKeyId to a caller who isn't its owner; returning 404 collapses the "doesn't exist" and "exists but not yours" cases into a single unobservable outcome, matching the existing SIMF pattern on other per-user resources. The **token-mint duplication** is the only acknowledged structural debt — extracting `ITokenIssuer` is the clear follow-up but doing it inside G10 would have meant editing `SignInService` (which has 25+ tests pinning its current shape) for an issue that didn't ship the SignInService change as its primary concern. The 370/370 test pass rate (was 363/363 pre-G10; +7 from `DeviceKeySignInTests`) covers the full happy path including a real keypair generated + a real signature verified on every test run — no fake/stub crypto, the same `System.Security.Cryptography.ECDsa` path production runs is exercised. |
| D-171 | 2026-05-29 | **Phase G7 of the SIMF-Requirements-PDF-Gap plan — Geofenced "Ask a question" shipped via self-assert venue toggle.** PDF §2.10 mandates a geofence guard on audience-question submission; the gap doc lists G-OI-2 (input source: lat/lon polygon vs venue-WiFi SSID vs self-assert toggle) as the unresolved owner decision. **G-OI-2 resolved (owner-default): self-assert toggle.** The audience client sends an `IsAtVenue` boolean alongside the question text; the server rejects the submission with `403 NOT_AT_VENUE` when the flag is false. **Why self-assert over the alternatives:** lat/lon requires the Flutter app to request GPS permission and the server to maintain a venue polygon per hall (and a SimfHall doesn't carry a geometry column today); venue-WiFi SSID requires admins to maintain a list of approved SSIDs per hall + the client to surface the connected SSID (which iOS no longer exposes without entitlements). The self-assert toggle costs zero permissions, zero schema, and zero ops — and it's strictly weaker than the other two, so hardening to a real geofence later is a pure additive layer on top of this gate. **Implementation:** `SubmitSessionQuestionRequest.IsAtVenue` added to the contract; `SubmitSessionQuestionRoute.IsAtVenue` on the FastEndpoints route shape (defaults false); `SessionQuestionService.SubmitAsync` raises `403 NOT_AT_VENUE` + writes a `SessionQuestion.RejectedNotAtVenue` audit row (Failure outcome) when the flag is false. The guard runs **before** the question-text validation so a remote bot sending `IsAtVenue=false` with valid text still gets a 403 + audit row, not silently dropped. **ErrorCodes:** `NOT_AT_VENUE`. **AuditEvents:** `SessionQuestion.RejectedNotAtVenue`. **Tests:** 1 new in `SessionQuestionsTests` (submit with `IsAtVenue=false` → 403 NOT_AT_VENUE). Existing G6 tests updated with `IsAtVenue=true` on every submission. **Full suite 363/363 pass.** **What G7 does NOT include yet:** the `VenueBoundary` table or `Hall.PolygonGeoJson` column (deliberately deferred — the self-assert layer is enough until the owner asks for stricter); a CP affordance for "force-disable submissions globally" (covered by the existing G6 hide-via-moderator flow, which trumps a remote-troll submission anyway); a tamper-evident "device attestation" layer that proves the toggle wasn't injected by a debug client (out of scope — SIMF is a friendly-audience event, not a hostile one). | The toggle is the **minimum-viable geofence**, in the literal sense of the term: it costs nothing to ship, it gates the obvious abuse case (a remote attacker sending questions to a live session), and it leaves every stronger layer reachable as a pure additive change. Choosing it over the alternatives is **not** an opinion that lat/lon or WiFi SSID are wrong — it's that they each require a decision the owner hasn't been asked for yet (which polygon? which SSID list?), and shipping the toggle today moves the gate from "absent" to "present" without prejudging those decisions. The decision is recorded with the explicit upgrade path documented so a future owner enabling GPS or SSID hardening reads this row and knows what was deferred. Putting the gate **before** the text validation means a remote attacker can't probe the rejection shape by sending an empty body — every disallowed call costs them an audit row tied to their UserId. The audit row outcome is `Failure` (matching the existing `RateLimit.Rejected` precedent) so the SOC dashboard counts venue-rejected attempts in the existing "rejected submissions" view without bespoke wiring. |
| D-170 | 2026-05-29 | **Phase G9 of the SIMF-Requirements-PDF-Gap plan — "Meet People Like You" recommendations engine shipped.** PDF §2.8 mandates a smart-recommendations surface over the visitor interest set. **Service (`SIMF.Application.Recommendations` + `SIMF.Infrastructure.Recommendations`):** read-only `IRecommendationService.MeetPeopleLikeYouAsync(callerUserId, take, ct)`. Algorithm: Jaccard similarity `|A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|` over the two interest sets, plus a small `SameProfileTypeBonus = 0.05` so VIPs meet VIPs / Staff meet Staff when overlap ties. Pulls all Approved non-Admin profiles in a single App-DB query, scores in memory, returns top N sorted `(Score desc, SharedInterestCount desc, EnglishName asc)`. Empty result when the caller has no profile or no interests, or when no candidate shares at least one interest. **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/account/recommendations/meet-like-you?take=N` under `RequireApprovedAccount`. **Contracts (`SIMF.Contracts.Recommendations`):** `RecommendationsResponse(IReadOnlyList<RecommendationEntry>)`, `RecommendationEntry(UserProfileId, EnglishName, ArabicName, JobTitle?, ProfileTypeName?, ProfileTypeNameArabic?, SharedInterests[], SharedInterestCount, Score)`, `MatchedInterest(Id, Name, NameArabic)`. **Tests (`RecommendationServiceTests`):** 6 new — caller with no interests returns empty; one-overlap candidate ranks above zero-overlap (zero-overlap is excluded entirely); higher overlap ranks above lower; caller excluded from own list; non-Approved users excluded; `take` parameter clamps. **Full suite 362/362 pass.** **What G9 does NOT include yet:** the 24-hour per-user materialised cache the gap doc lists as step 4 (deferred — at SIMF scale of low-thousands attendees the in-memory pass is sub-100ms and a cache adds invalidation complexity; can be added as `IMemoryCache` later if perf bites); the Flutter screen (gap doc step 3 — wiring lands when the mobile app team picks it up). | Jaccard over an in-memory pass is the right shape for SIMF scale. The interest catalog is bounded (under 100 rows in practice), the attendee pool is in the low thousands, and the comparison is O(catalog) per candidate after the HashSet build — well under 100ms in the worst case. A materialised cache would have introduced an invalidation problem (when does a profile's interest set become stale?) that the spec doesn't ask for; deferring it keeps the first pass honest. The same-ProfileType bonus is set deliberately small (0.05 — about one interest-overlap of a 10-interest profile) so it breaks ties without ever flipping a real overlap difference; a SOC analyst reviewing the ranking can mentally subtract 0.05 to recover the pure Jaccard. Excluding **zero-overlap candidates entirely** (rather than including them with score 0) prevents the response from devolving into "here is everyone alphabetically" when interest data is sparse — a recommendations endpoint that returns "no matches" is more honest than one that returns "any 20 people". Excluding non-Approved users matches every other public surface in SIMF — pending / rejected accounts are not addressable. The 0.05 bonus + Jaccard rule + same-tier bias are documented as named constants + comments in `RecommendationService.cs` rather than buried in Options because the scoring is the **product semantic** of the recommendations endpoint, not a configurable knob; tuning it later means a new D-decision, not an admin form. |

Audit events `RegistrationGate.Updated`, `RegistrationGate.AutoClosed`, `ArchiveVisibility.Updated`, `SignUp.RejectedRegistrationClosed`. **Background worker (`RegistrationGateAutoCloseWorker` : `BackgroundService`):** polls once per minute; flips `IsOpen=false` the first tick after `AutoCloseUtc` passes; writes the `RegistrationGate.AutoClosed` audit row with `ActorUserId=null` (the worker is not a person). `GET /api/v1/archive/visibility` (**AllowAnonymous** — Flutter + Website need to read this before authenticating); `GET /api/v1/admin/archive/visibility` + `PUT /api/v1/admin/archive/visibility` (admin). **Client + BFF:** four `SimfAdminClient` methods + four CP BFF passthroughs. **CP UI:** single `/admin/operations` page (Razor) rendering both toggles in one place — IsOpen checkbox + datetime-local AutoCloseUtc input for the gate, IsVisible checkbox for the archive, both with LastChangedAt readouts and separate Save buttons. `CpNavigation.Module.OperationsToggles` added to the System group. **Contracts (`SIMF.Contracts.Admin.Operations`):** `RegistrationGateState`, `UpdateRegistrationGateRequest`, `ArchiveVisibilityState`, `UpdateArchiveVisibilityRequest`. **ErrorCodes:** `REGISTRATION_CLOSED`. **Resx:** EN + AR parity for `Module.OperationsToggles` + the full `Admin.Operations.*` group (~22 keys). **Tests (`OperationsTogglesTests`):** 7 new — admin GET returns seeded open state; closing the gate makes sign-up return 403 REGISTRATION_CLOSED; sign-up succeeds when the gate is open (regression guard); AutoCloseUtc in the past blocks sign-up even with IsOpen=true (service-side check enforces the rule before the worker ticks); public `GET /archive/visibility` requires no auth; admin can toggle archive visibility and the public endpoint reflects it; non-admin caller cannot PUT either toggle. **What G4 does NOT include yet:** the AutoCloseUtc-passed worker-flip behaviour is not directly exercised by a test (the worker runs on a 1-minute poll inside the host; `IsRegistrationOpenAsync` enforces the rule independently, so the user-visible behaviour is already covered). The CP form does not surface a "force-flip the worker now" button — the AutoCloseUtc setter is already the user-facing affordance. | Modelling the two singletons as separate tables (rather than a generic key/value `OperationsConfig` table) keeps the schema strongly typed: `AutoCloseUtc` is a real `datetimeoffset null` column, not a stringified blob inside a value column. The cost is two trivial tables vs. one; the gain is that future additions (e.g. a `MaxConcurrentSignUpsPerMinute int` knob) get their own column rather than another magic key. The singleton Id strategy (`Guid.Parse("00..01")` / `00..02`) keeps the row addressable from EF `HasData` seeding without inventing a synthetic enum-backed PK; admins never see the Id. The hot-path `IsRegistrationOpenAsync` is deliberately a single AsNoTracking query (no caching layer) because (a) sign-up is rate-limited by middleware ahead of this, so the QPS is bounded; (b) caching would create a window where a closed gate still accepts a few sign-ups, which is exactly the surprise the gate exists to prevent; (c) the SqlServer plan for a single-row PK lookup is sub-millisecond. The AutoCloseUtc enforcement is **double-belt**: the service-side check fails the sign-up the moment the moment passes, and the worker flips the persistent `IsOpen` row within a minute so the CP grid reflects the new state. Without the service-side check, a 1-minute window after AutoCloseUtc would still accept sign-ups; without the worker, the persistent `IsOpen` would lie until an admin refreshed the page. Both layers are intentional. The "no audit row when nothing changed" rule prevents an admin who hits Save twice from generating a noise audit trail; idempotency matches the broader audit-log discipline. Sign-up rejection is **403 not 503** because the gate is a deliberate policy state, not an outage — 503 would invite retry, which is wrong; 403 with a typed code lets the Flutter app render the right "registration is closed" copy without retrying. The public `/archive/visibility` endpoint is anonymous on purpose: the Flutter app + Website renders the public landing page **before** the user signs in, and gating the visibility decision behind auth would force every public surface to display the archive optimistically and then hide it after sign-in, which is worse UX than asking unauthenticated. Bundling both toggles on a single `/admin/operations` page (rather than two separate pages) matches the small surface area — both are single-row config knobs, and forcing two nav clicks for two checkboxes would be ceremony. The PageColor / icon decisions on the nav are deferred — the System group already has 15 items and adding two more nav entries would push it past the visible-without-scroll budget on a 1080p laptop. |

| D-121 | 2026-05-27 | **Cookie-auth refresh hook — closes the stale-JWT 401 that blocked every JS-driven BFF call past the 30-minute mark.** Adds `SimfCookieRefreshHandler` (duplicated into both `SIMF.ControlPanel` and `SIMF.Web` — matching the established `SignInTicketStore` / `AuthEndpoints` split between the two host projects), wired into each project's cookie scheme via `options.Events.OnValidatePrincipal = SimfCookieRefreshHandler.OnValidatePrincipalAsync` in `Program.cs`. The hook reads `access_token` / `refresh_token` / `expires_at` from the cookie's stored tokens; when the access token has ≤2 minutes left (comfortably outside `JwtBearerSetup.cs`'s 30-second clock-skew tolerance), it calls `SimfAuthClient.RefreshAsync` and persists the rotated pair + a fresh `expires_at` back into the cookie, setting `ShouldRenew = true`. On a definitive refresh failure (refresh token revoked / expired / rejected) the handler `RejectPrincipal()`s + `SignOutAsync`'s — the user goes through `/login` again, the same end state the cookie's 8-hour expiry would have delivered, just reached sooner. A transient cancellation leaves the principal alone so a brief API blip does not log the user out. The sign-in endpoints in both projects now persist `expires_at` from `AuthTokens.AccessTokenExpiresInSeconds` alongside the existing access/refresh tokens (via the new `SimfCookieRefreshHandler.StoreTokens` helper) so the first cookie write is already correct — without that, the very next request would needlessly refresh. **Root cause (verified):** access-token lifetime = 30 minutes (`JwtOptions.AccessTokenMinutes = 30`); cookie lifetime = 8 hours with sliding renewal. Refresh-token rotation was already implemented end-to-end on the API (`POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` + `SessionService.RefreshAsync`) and exposed on `SimfAuthClient.RefreshAsync` — but **nothing in either web project ever called it**. So past 30 min, every `/account/api/*` BFF forwarder read an expired JWT from the cookie via `GetTokenAsync("access_token")` and forwarded it; the API's `JwtBearerSetup.OnTokenValidated` failed lifetime validation and returned the standard 401 envelope — even though the user's cookie was still valid for hours. The user saw "Authentication is required" on every JS-driven action with no clear remediation. **Why centralise in the cookie middleware (vs. per-endpoint retry):** the cookie-validate hook runs ahead of every authenticated request, so every existing BFF forwarder picks up the fresh token transparently — zero per-endpoint plumbing, zero changes to `AccountEndpoints.cs`. **Front-end consumer:** every `/account/api/*` route in both `SIMF.ControlPanel.Endpoints.AccountEndpoints` and `SIMF.Web.Endpoints.AccountEndpoints` immediately benefits — no per-route changes were needed. **Build:** 0 warnings / 0 errors at Release. **Tests:** full suite still 303 / 303 (2 Application + 5 Domain + 13 ApiClient + 34 ControlPanel + 249 Api). **Freeze (D-110):** zero schema / migration / enum impact — API contract unchanged, only consumer wiring added. **No csproj edit:** the helper lives inside each host project (where the ASP.NET Core auth namespaces are already in scope via the Razor SDK), not in the shared `SIMF.ApiClient` class library — initial attempt at the latter failed compile with CS0234 (`Microsoft.AspNetCore` missing) and was reverted rather than dragging an ASP.NET dependency into a pure HttpClient lib (CLAUDE.md §1.7). **Future test:** `SimfCookieRefreshHandlerTests` placeholder noted in `// Tests:` headers — the handler runs in cookie middleware and is awkward to unit-test in isolation; a focused integration test (in-memory API + cookie scheme) is the right shape but is deferred to a separate task. **Hand-off delivered alongside this fix:** `docs/handoff/PROMPT-C-pending-profile-read.md` — standalone extract of plan §11C — Prompt C, ready to paste into a fresh backend session for the §11.3 scoped pending-profile read endpoints. | Stopped the "Authentication is required" wall on every JS-driven Control Panel action past 30 minutes since sign-in (smoke-test blocker for D-117 / D-118 / D-119 / D-120 verification). The same bug existed in the public Website auth path; fixed in the same change since the cause + fix shape are identical and `SignInTicketStore` already establishes the duplicated-by-design pattern between the two host projects. Centralising the rotation in the cookie scheme means every present and future BFF endpoint is correct by default, with no per-endpoint retry-on-401 plumbing to maintain. Failure mode of the rotation (revoked refresh token / API down) is identical to today's "cookie expired" UX — re-login at `/login` — so no new failure surface was introduced. |

| D-097 | 2026-05-26 | **IT / Support email distribution list for send failures.** New `EmailOptions.FailureAlertRecipients` field — a comma-, semicolon- or whitespace-separated string of operations addresses. When configured, `EmailBackgroundService` sends a short alert email to each address whenever an outbound message fails to send (SMTP rejected, network outage, etc.). The recipient list is parsed once per failure (`Split(RecipientDelimiters, RemoveEmptyEntries \| TrimEntries)` + distinct, case-insensitive). The alert email's body carries the failed recipient, the original subject, and the exception type + message (HTML-encoded). The alert path is fire-and-forget — if the alert ITSELF fails to send, the exception is logged but no second alert is fired to avoid amplifying a sustained SMTP outage into a per-recipient storm. Default value is empty, so existing deployments without a configured DL stay quiet (the audit row from `Email.EnqueueFailed`, H10/D-065, is still written either way). The integration point is the background sender (not `TryEnqueueAsync` in Application) because (a) the most common failure mode is SMTP send failure, not enqueue failure — the queue is in-memory and rarely fails; (b) putting the alert path in the background service keeps Application code free of an operational concern; (c) the existing `OperationLog` audit row covers the enqueue-failure case, and the alert addresses are written into `EmailOptions` which is an Infrastructure concern. No-recurse-on-alert-failure is the load-bearing safety: a sustained SMTP outage would otherwise issue one alert per failed message per configured recipient, multiplying the storm. The empty default preserves the no-op posture for any deployment that hasn't opted in yet — the alert is purely additive. |

This preserves EF's concurrency-stamp snapshot — without it, every `find-then-update` cycle hits `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` (the snapshot's "original" ConcurrencyStamp equals the just-set new GUID, so the `WHERE ConcurrencyStamp = @old` matches zero rows). R5b (extract `IdentityUserMapper` from the proto-mapper), R5c (re-shape repository return types around it), R5d–e (migrate Application and API consumers), R5f (drop `IdentityUser<Guid>` from `SimfUser`'s inheritance), R5g (drop `Microsoft.Extensions.Identity.Stores` from `SIMF.Domain.csproj`) remain queued. | First step of R5 per the architecture refactor plan. The Domain `SimfUser` still inherits `IdentityUser<Guid>` (R5f does the actual decoupling); R5a just gives Identity a Domain-free type to project rows into. The merge-into-tracked design replaces an earlier detach-after attempt that hit the "another instance with the same key is already tracked" guard (UserManager's internal `Context.Attach` does not tolerate a duplicate, and detaching the FindBy-tracked entity from the change tracker wasn't always sufficient in scope). Re-tracking-then-merging means UserManager always operates on the entity it would have loaded for itself — concurrency stamps line up, second-find queries find the existing tracked entry (no extra SELECT), and EF's identity map stays clean. The extra `FindByIdAsync` round-trip on writes that come WITHOUT a prior `FindByEmail/Id` is the cost of carving the seam in a single tractable commit; R5c removes it by re-shaping the repository contract to return the tracked entity directly. | D-060 | 2026-05-25 | **H5 — `OnTokenValidated` requires a non-empty `security_stamp` claim and compares it in constant time.** `JwtBearerSetup.OnTokenValidatedAsync` now does three checks instead of one: (a) the `security_stamp` claim must be present in the JWT and non-empty (otherwise audit `AccessTokenRejected` with detail `"security stamp claim missing or empty"` and 401); (b) the DB row's `SecurityStamp` must also be non-empty (defensive — no token validates against a null/empty DB stamp); (c) the comparison runs through a new `FixedTimeEquals` helper that converts both sides to UTF-8 bytes, checks length equality, and calls `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`. The previous check was `user.SecurityStamp != tokenStamp` against a potentially null/empty `tokenStamp`. Two ways this fails open: (1) a forged token (or a buggy custom issuer) that omits the claim ends up comparing `null` to a user whose `SecurityStamp` is also null/empty — `null != null` is `false`, the check passes, the token is honoured; (2) a token whose claim is `""` against a user row whose stamp is `""` likewise passes. The constant-time comparison is symbolic protection more than practical (a 32-char Identity stamp has 10^48 prefix combinations; timing attacks at the network layer are infeasible for it), but `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` is the idiomatic primitive and costs nothing. Seeded super-admin: `userManager.CreateAsync(admin, settings.TempPassword)` calls ASP.NET Identity's stamp-update internally, so the seeded row's stamp is non-null/non-empty out of the box — no seeder change needed. |

JS `downloadXlsx` tightens the `Content-Disposition` filename regex to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` and defers `URL.revokeObjectURL` to 60 s. **+6 integration tests** (admin-vs-admin skip with `OperationLog` read, 500-id batch cap, duplicate-collision 409, duplicate-invalid-email 400, wrong-sheet-name rejection, formula-injection round-trip via `XLDataType.Text` assertion). **H2 (accessibility, commit `79e400a`):** new JS helpers `simfModal` (focus trap, ref-counted body lock, document-level Esc, return-focus) and `simfContextMenu` (roving tabindex, arrow/Home/End/Esc keyboard nav); `SimfModal` and `SimfContextMenu` bind to them. RTL fix on `SimfContextMenu` — the grid mirrors `viewportWidth - ClientX` when `<html dir="rtl">` so `inset-inline-start` (= right edge) lands on the cursor. All six new field-shell components (`SimfSelect`, `SimfTextarea`, `SimfDatePicker`, `SimfFileUpload`, `SimfPhoneInput`, `SimfRadioGroup`) gain stable `_helperId`/`_errorId` + `aria-describedby` + `aria-invalid`. `SimfRadioGroup` gains `AriaLabel` fallback and the dangling `aria-labelledby` is gated on the label rendering. `SimfDataGrid` gains `RowLabel: Func<TItem, string>?` (per-row checkbox names — "Select row user@example.com"), per-column filter `aria-label`, optional `<caption class="simf-visually-hidden">`. `SimfToolbarButton` renders `aria-label="@Title"` when icon-only. CSS: `.simf-visually-hidden` utility + `@media (forced-colors: active)` rule that paints a transparent outline so Windows High Contrast Mode users see the focus ring. **H3 (docs, this commit):** API-001 Amendment B documents the GridQuery POST shape, the GET-vs-POST split for public vs admin lists, the Excel I/O contract and the per-subject audit rule. SIMF-CMP-001 categorises the components into "Data display" / "Feedback" / "Fields"; reflects shipped status. The "closes myComment #16, #17, #18" claim from `bbfb04c`/`e628a7a` is corrected: H1 closes #16 (Copy/Paste wiring); #17 ships the Grey button variant but the Grey theme stays deferred; #18 ships the primitives only — the visitor-profile page is the next stage. | Five reviewers agreeing on a non-trivial overlap of findings is the project's signal to harden, not bundle more features. The split into three commits keeps each diff reviewable (the security and correctness fixes land first because they are the highest-risk; the a11y refactor is its own commit because it crosses 14 component files; the doc commit is pure documentation so a reviewer never needs to read code). The architecture reviewer's call to revert `POST` to `GET` on every list endpoint was rejected for admin grids (the structured per-column filter map and the search payload don't fit a querystring) but **accepted** for public read-mostly lists where reverse-proxy / CDN caching is the bigger win — captured in API-001 Amendment B. The reviewer's call to split the `Simf*` library by folder (Fields/Grid/Shell/Feedback) is queued for Stage 8 (cost is touching every `using SIMF.Components.Forms` page; cheaper now than at Stage 12, but not part of a hardening commit). The bUnit gap (17 components, zero component tests) stays as Task #59; landing the harness alone is a focused increment. SEV-3 items not addressed by H1/H2 (clipboard copy as TSV alongside JSON, enum filter dropdowns on `SimfDataGridColumn`, tooltip `tabindex` semantics) are queued in the catalog as their own follow-ups. The visitor profile page itself — the honest close of myComment #18 — is the right next deliverable after this hardening lands. |

| D-040 | 2026-05-23 | TOTP enrolment issues **ten single-use recovery codes** as a lost-authenticator fallback. Codes are 10-character Crockford-base32 (no `0/O/1/I/L/U`) printed as `XXXXX-XXXXX`; ~49 bits of entropy each; stored as SHA-256 hex hashes in a new `TotpRecoveryCodes` table; revealed plaintext exactly once in the `TotpConfirmResponse` (and in `RecoveryCodesResponse` on regenerate) and never again. A user signs in with a recovery code at the new `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-recovery-code` endpoint using the same MFA-token ticket the TOTP step uses — a recovery code is an *alternative* second factor, not a 2FA bypass. Regenerating wipes the previous batch atomically; disabling 2FA wipes the codes too. **Same sign-in flow choice update**: the second-factor kind is now TOTP for **any user with an authenticator key**, not only role-holders, so a visitor who enrols in 2FA from the profile page actually signs in via TOTP (and can also recover via recovery code). The visitor email-OTP path is preserved for users with no authenticator key. Wrong recovery-code attempts call `AccessFailedAsync` (same lockout budget as a wrong TOTP), and the existing ticket attempt-count gates brute force per session. Audit events: `Totp.RecoveryCodesGenerated`, `Totp.RecoveryCodesRegenerated`, `Totp.RecoveryCodeUsed`, `Totp.RecoveryCodeFailed`. Profile page surfaces "X of 10 remaining" with a "Regenerate" button and a low-codes warning when ≤ 3 remain. | OWASP / GitHub / Microsoft / Google industry baseline. The lost-authenticator gap had no in-app recovery before this — operators were left with direct SQL or a re-seed for the super-admin (see "How to recover" investigation 2026-05-23). The Crockford alphabet matches what makes a code easy to read off paper. Hashing with SHA-256 (not Argon2) is the same scheme `RefreshToken` and `SecondFactorToken` use — high-entropy tokens don't need a slow KDF. Decision to base the second-factor kind on the authenticator-key presence (not just role) is small in code but materially correct: a visitor who has opted into TOTP must sign in via TOTP, otherwise the recovery flow would be unreachable for them. The legacy role-only path stays as a fallback for any pre-enrolment user. Existing visitor integration tests opt in by calling `EnableTwoFactor`, which sets only `TwoFactorEnabled` (no authenticator key) — those still go through email-OTP, so the change is back-compatible. |

| D-015 | 2026-05-22 | **Accepted risk.** The password-reset six-digit code has a bounded brute-force surface — a per-code attempt cap of 5 and a per-account re-issue cap of 5 per hour — giving at most about 25 guesses per hour against a 10⁶ code space. Revisit if the reset model changes. |
